info.title: Truto API
info.description: Truto's Admin API is the control plane for the entire Truto platform. Use it to manage integrations and integrated accounts, environments, unified models, sync jobs and templates, datastores, webhooks, workflows, API tokens, static gates, MCP servers, and more.

SessionCookie.name: session
SessionCookie.description:
Browser session cookie issued by the login flows. Used by the passkey registration and management endpoints, which are session-only — an API token is rejected with 403.
Host-scoped: issued with no `Domain` attribute, so it is sent back only to the exact API host that set it and never to a sibling origin.

value.description: Null when there is nothing to measure, e.g. a rate with no requests behind it.

previous.description: The same figure for the span of equal length just before the range (ending at the same time of day); null when that span is not inside the 90-day window, and for numbers that describe the accounts as they are now.

series.description: One value per day of the range (null for a rate or latency with no requests that day); empty for numbers that describe the accounts as they are now.

ForbiddenErrorInsightSchema.description:
Present on a 403 from the provider, on both the Unified and Proxy APIs. Not every 403 is a
scope problem: `value.refusal_basis` states what Truto can say the refusal rests on.

Truto does not summarise the integration's error body. It travels beside this insight,
verbatim and unranked, as `raw_response` — and on the durable record as
`raw_response_excerpt`. Read that for the provider's own account of the refusal; read this
for Truto's.

description.description: A sentence derived from `value.refusal_basis`, safe to show a reader as-is.
description.example: Access forbidden. This connection does not hold every scope this resource and method requires — reconnect and grant the scopes listed alongside this error.

refusal_basis.description:
Always present. **Treat this as an open set**: the values below are the ones Truto
emits today, and the read path deliberately accepts an unrecognised one so a newly
shipped state cannot break a client — or an older Truto build — that has not heard
of it. Generate a permissive type from it and keep a default branch.

`scopes_missing` — the scopes in `missing_scopes` are absent from the grant, and a
re-consent flow is the remedy. `scopes_satisfied` — every declared scope is
granted, so the refusal has another cause. `non_scope_requirement` — the
requirement is a role or API-key permission, named in `required_permissions`, so
reconnecting will not change it. `no_scope_concept` — this connection's auth method
has no OAuth scopes at all, so there is nothing to grant and reconnecting cannot
help. `not_determined` — no comparison ran and Truto cannot name a basis; read
`description` for which of the reasons applied, and `raw_response` for the
provider's own account.

Each value leads somewhere different, in what a reader is told AND in what remedy
is worth offering. Where two states differed only in why Truto had no answer they
are one state here, and the difference survives in `description`.

A closed `enum` here, unlike on `last_forbidden_error.refusal_basis`, because a
running build always emits its own documented set — this value is computed per
request, never read back from storage. A build that ships a sixth state ships this
list with it.

missing_scopes.description:
Declared all-of scopes absent from the grant. Present only for `scopes_missing`
and `scopes_satisfied`. Do not default an absent value to `[]` — absent means no
comparison ran, which is not the same statement as "nothing is missing".

missing_any_of_scopes.description: Scopes of which the operation needs any one, where the grant holds none.

required_permissions.description:
What the operation requires, whether or not a comparison was possible. Always
paired with `permission_vocabulary`.

required_any_of_permissions.description: Permissions of which the operation needs any one.

permission_vocabulary.description:
Which vocabulary the required permissions are written in, and therefore what the
remedy is. Only `oauth_scope` is fixed by reconnecting.

TrutoErrorInsightSchema.description:
The `truto_error_insight` object on an error response body. Every key is optional and
which ones appear depends on the failure; see the Errors guide for the full list. The
Proxy API has no unified schema to compare a request against, so only `forbidden_error`
is added there.

RemoteErrorResponseSchema.description:
The body Truto returns when a **third-party API** refused the call, rather than Truto
itself. Identified by `truto_is_remote_error`.

This is the envelope `truto_error_insight` arrives in. It is a **`components/schemas`
entry that no operation references**, deliberately, and the reason is worth stating so it
is not "fixed" by hanging it off an unrelated route: the operations that return it are the
Unified API and Proxy API data routes, and neither is enumerated here. The Unified API's
paths and payloads are generated per unified model and per integration, so there is no
fixed operation to attach. The Proxy API's paths are fixed (`/proxy/{resource}`) but are
not documented in this specification at all — a pre-existing gap, and documenting them is
its own piece of work.

A `components/responses` wrapper used to sit beside this. It was removed: nothing could
reference it either, so it added a second unreachable node rather than a route into this
one. Mainstream generators emit every `components/schemas` entry as a named type whether or
not a path reaches it, so this shape is importable today; a generator that prunes
unreferenced schemas will not see it, and until the routes above are documented that is the
honest state of affairs rather than something a `$ref` can paper over.

The shape itself is fixed, and is what a client should type those calls against. See the
Errors guide for the full list of insight keys.

message.description:
The human text pulled out of the provider's own error body.

**Unbounded, and not always a sentence.** The extractor's last candidate is the payload
itself when the payload is a string, so for a plain-text or HTML error body this field
is the entire body — 34 KB is a real observed value. Size it accordingly, or truncate
before display. `raw_response_excerpt` on `last_forbidden_error` is the only capped
copy of a provider body Truto stores.

truto_is_remote_error.description:
`true` when the third-party API produced this error. When absent or `false`, Truto
rejected the request before it left the edge.

raw_response.description:
The integration's error body, verbatim and uninterpreted. An object for a JSON body, a
string for a plain-text or HTML one. Present on every remote error.

BatchRequestSchema.description: The request body for creating a batch request, containing an integrated account ID and an array of resources.

BatchRequestResponse.description:
The combined response returned by `POST /batch-request`. Successful resource
records are grouped under `result`, keyed by the `name` of each resource in
the request. Errors are surfaced under `errors`, keyed the same way.

result.description:
Map of resource names to the records fetched for that resource. The key
is the resource's `name` from the request body.

oneOf.description: A JSON record returned for the resource.
Raw text or base64 payload when the upstream response is not JSON (for example, a file).

errors.description:
Map of resource names to errors encountered while processing that
resource. Present only for resources that failed.

error.description: Serialized error object describing what went wrong.

retryAfter.description: Milliseconds to wait before retrying. Set when the upstream API returned a rate-limit response.

LogBase.description:
Common fields present on every log entry returned by `GET /log`. Each
concrete variant (e.g. `UnifiedProxyApiLog`, `WebhookLog`) extends this
base with type-specific fields via `allOf`.

timestamp.description: The time at which the log entry was recorded.

message.description: Human-readable summary of the log event.

service.description: The service that generated the log.

app_env.description:
The deployment that wrote the log (`production`, `staging`,
`staging2`, `thoropass-production`, and per-developer preview
deployments). Distinct from `environment_id`, which is the Truto
environment the log belongs to: a single `environment_id` can be
served by more than one deployment, and `app_env` is what tells
them apart. Not an enumerated set — new deployments add values.

environment_id.description: The Truto environment in which the log was generated.

log_type.description:
Discriminator. Echoed from the `log_type` query parameter so each
row is self-describing. Use this to switch on variant when
consuming the response programmatically.

logs.description: Internal log messages captured during request/job processing.
example: Token still valid — no refresh needed

HttpRequestFields.description:
HTTP request/response context shared by log types that originate from
an inbound HTTP request (`unified_proxy_api` and `mcp`).

host.description: The hostname that served the request.

http_url.description: The full URL of the request (with sensitive paths masked).

http_status_code.description: The HTTP status code of the response.

http_method.description: The HTTP method of the request.

http_ip.description: The IP address of the client.

http_request_id.description: The Cloudflare Ray ID for the request.

http_country.description: The country code of the client (from Cloudflare).

http_useragent.description: The User-Agent header of the request.

http_url_details_host.description: The hostname portion of the request URL.

http_url_details_path.description:
The path portion of the request URL. On `mcp` rows the token
segment is masked in full, so the value is always
`/mcp/[redacted]` and identifies nothing — use
`mcp_server_id` / `mcp_server_name` instead.

http_url_details_query_string.description: The parsed query string parameters of the request URL.

user_id.description: The ID of the authenticated user, if applicable.

response_headers.description: The response headers returned to the client.

Log entry produced by an inbound request to the Unified API or Proxy
API. Use `request_type` to distinguish a unified-mapping call from a
raw proxy passthrough.

request_type.description: Whether the request was served by a Unified API mapping or a raw Proxy API passthrough.

duration.description: Total time in milliseconds between Truto receiving the request and sending the response.

fetch_duration.description: Time in milliseconds spent fetching data from the upstream API.

integrated_account_id.description: The integrated account that the request was made against.

integration.description: The integration name that handled the request.

method.description: The Truto method that was called (`list`, `get`, `create`, `update`, `delete`, or a custom method name).

resource.description: The Truto resource that was called.

remote_requests.description: Upstream HTTP requests made to third-party APIs during processing.

integrated_account_needs_reauth.description: Whether the integrated account's credentials need to be refreshed.

result_count.description: The number of results returned by a list operation.

McpLog.description: Log entry produced by an MCP request handled by Truto's MCP server.

duration.description: Total time in milliseconds between Truto receiving the MCP request and sending the response.

fetch_duration.description: Time in milliseconds spent fetching data from the upstream API while servicing the MCP request.

integrated_account_id.description: The integrated account this MCP server is bound to.

integration.description: The integration name that handled the MCP request.

client_name.description: The name of the MCP client.

client_version.description: The version of the MCP client.

tool_name.description: The MCP tool that was called (only set for `tools/call`).

resource.description: The Truto resource backing the called tool.

method.description: The Truto method backing the called tool.

RapidBridgeLog.description:
Log entry produced by a RapidBridge sync job run. These logs come from
Durable Objects that drive sync jobs (rather than from inbound HTTP
requests).

durable_object.description: The Durable Object class that emitted the log.

integrated_account_id.description: The integrated account the sync job is running against.

integration.description: The integration the sync job is running against.

sync_job_id.description: The sync job that was triggered.

sync_job_run_event.description:
The lifecycle event being logged for the sync job run. This is
the field that carries run outcome on this log type — there is
no `status` field on these rows.

version.description: The sync-job runtime version that produced the run.

resource.description: The resource this sync step fetched or transformed.

method.description:
Ambiguous by design — this stream is written by two loggers.
On a row emitted by the Durable Object's own logger (the
`fetch` entrypoint) this is the **HTTP verb** the object was
invoked with (`PUT`, `DELETE`). On a per-request row (the bulk
of the stream) it is the **Truto method** executed by that sync
step (`list`, `get`, `create`, ...), and is paired with
`resource`. Rows emitted by the alarm entrypoint carry no
`method` at all.

num_records.description: The number of records produced by this sync step.

fetch_duration.description: Time in milliseconds spent fetching data from the upstream API for this sync step.

webhook_id.description: When the sync job was triggered by a webhook, the originating webhook ID.

webhook_status.description:
The HTTP status code returned when the sync job posted to its
configured webhook. Unrelated to the outcome of the run itself.

WebhookLog.description:
Log entry produced when Truto delivers a webhook to a customer
endpoint. Delivery runs in the `webhook_delivery` Durable Object; the
`webhooks` queue only hands the event to that object and emits no logs
of its own, so these rows carry `durable_object`, not `queue`.

durable_object.description: The Durable Object class that emitted the log.

method.description:
Which delivery path emitted the row — `deliver` for the first
attempt, `alarm` for a scheduled retry. This is not a Truto API
method.

status.description:
Only ever set to `error`, on a failed or skipped delivery.
Absent on a successful delivery — read `webhook_endpoint_status`
for the endpoint's response code.

event_type.description:
The event that triggered the webhook delivery. Filter on it with
the `event` key of `log_type_filter`.

integrated_account_id.description: The integrated account the event originated from, when the payload identifies one.

integration.description: The integration slug the event originated from, when the payload identifies one.

webhook_endpoint_status.description: The HTTP status code returned by the customer's webhook endpoint. Absent for connection-level failures, where no HTTP response was received.

SyncJobCronTriggerLog.description:
Log entry produced when a sync job's cron alarm fires (one row per
scheduled sync trigger). The Alarm Durable Object delivers the tick as
an inbound `POST /alarm`, so these rows also carry the HTTP fields of
that internal call — `http_status_code` reflects whether Truto accepted
the tick, not anything about the upstream integration.

This is the only log type that takes no `log_type_filter` keys beyond
the implicit environment scope.

alarm_type.description: The alarm classifier emitted by the underlying Durable Object.

entity_id.description: The sync job cron trigger whose alarm fired.

http_status_code.description: The status Truto returned for the internal alarm delivery. `200` means the tick was accepted and a sync job run was created.

http_method.description: The HTTP method of the internal alarm delivery. Always `POST`.

duration.description: Time in milliseconds Truto spent handling the alarm tick.

Log.description:
A single log entry returned by `GET /log`. The `log_type` field on each
row matches the `log_type` query parameter that was used to fetch it,
and identifies which variant schema applies. Variants share the
`LogBase` fields and may carry additional fields not enumerated in the
spec — clients should treat unknown fields as opaque.

MCP.description:
An MCP server attached to an integrated account. Each integrated account can
have multiple MCP servers, each with its own scoping (`config.methods` and
`config.tags`), tool exposure mode, and optional expiry.

id.description: Unique identifier for the MCP server.

name.description: Human-readable name for the MCP server.

integrated_account_id.description: The integrated account this MCP server is bound to.

config.description: Optional scoping for the MCP server. When omitted, all available tools for the integrated account are exposed.

methods.description: Restrict the MCP server to these Truto method names. Combined with `tags` using AND semantics.

tags.description: Restrict the MCP server to tools whose effective tags (resource-level and optional resource.method tags) intersect these values.

tool_exposure.description:
How tools are exposed on `tools/list`.
- `all` (default): every matching tool schema is listed.
- `discovery`: only three meta-tools are listed (`search_tools`, `get_tool_schema`, `call_tool`). The client discovers and calls real tools through those.

require_api_token_auth.description: When true, MCP requests also require a valid Truto API token in the Authorization Bearer header.

expires_at.description: Optional expiry timestamp. When set, the MCP server's token is invalidated after this time.

created_by.description: ID of the user who created the MCP server.

created_at.description: Time at which the MCP server was created.

updated_at.description: Time at which the MCP server was last updated.

MCPCreateResponse.description:
Response returned by `POST /integrated-account/{integrated_account_id}/mcp`.
Includes the MCP server fields, the freshly minted bearer `token`, and the
full `url` to use when configuring an MCP client. The token is only returned
at creation time and cannot be retrieved later.

token.description: Bearer token used to authenticate MCP requests. Treat this as a secret; it is not retrievable after creation.

url.description: Full MCP endpoint URL. Configure your MCP client with this URL to connect to the server.

SyncJobRunState.description:
A key/value entry stored within a sync job's state namespace. Sync jobs use
this to persist incremental cursors, dedupe markers, and other small bits of

key.description: Key for this state entry. Unique within the namespace identified by `state_key`.

value.description: The stored value. Encode structured data (for example, JSON) as a string before storing.

sync_job_run_id.description: The ID of the sync job run that wrote this entry, if any.

created_at.description: Time at which the state entry was first created.

updated_at.description: Time at which the state entry was last updated.

environment_id.description: The environment to which this datastore belongs.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the datastore record was last updated.

webhook_type.description: The type of this webhook payload, if relevant (e.g. a "verify" event).

BillingInvoiceResponse.description: A Stripe invoice mirrored into Truto. Stripe remains the system of record; use `hosted_invoice_url` to view or pay it.

id.description: Truto's id for the mirrored invoice row.

source.description: `automated` when Truto generated it from a plan; `stripe_manual` when it was raised by hand in Stripe.

hosted_invoice_url.description: Stripe-hosted page to view and pay the invoice.

BillingPlanComponent.description: One pricing component of a plan. `usage` components bill measured usage in arrears; `fixed` components are recurring amounts billed in arrears once each cycle ends.

unit_price_cents.description: Price in cents (may be fractional) for one block of `unit_size` units, per interval. "$0.99 per 5,000 API calls" is `99` with `unit_size` 5000.

unit_size.description: Units per priced block. Overage is billed in whole blocks, rounded up. Default 1.

included_quantity.description: Units included before the unit price applies.

interval.description: How often the metric is billed; the unit price is per interval. Non-monthly metrics bill at the end of each cycle starting in `anchor_month`.

discount_percent.description: Percentage taken off this line; shown on the invoice as a separate discount line.

anchor_month.description: Non-monthly items only — the calendar month each cycle starts in.

billing_mode.description: `automatic` invoices are generated by the daily billing run on `billing_day`; `manual` plans are invoiced by Truto staff.

billing_day.description: Day of the month (UTC) automatic invoices are issued.

effective_from.description: First calendar month (always the 1st) this plan bills. Everything bills in arrears, so the first invoice is issued on `billing_day` of the following month.

billing_status.description: Informational; nothing is enforced on it today.

description.description: Invoice wording. Usage lines mention the included allowance only when the component has one.

quantity.description: Units charged; for usage lines the number of blocks of `unit_size`.

unit_price_cents.description: Price per charged unit (per block for usage lines).

unit_size.description: Usage lines only — units per block.

overage_quantity.description: Usage lines only — measured minus included, before block rounding.

period_end.description: Exclusive end (first day of the next period).

current_period.description: Month-to-date charges priced against the plan. Everything — platform fee, fixed items and usage — bills in arrears, so these are invoiced on `invoice_date`, after the month ends. `null` when the team has no active plan.

invoice_date.description: When these charges are invoiced, the plan's `billing_day` in the month after `period_end`. Null for manual plans and while the plan has not started.

next_invoice_date.description: Next date the daily billing run will invoice this team (its plan's `billing_day`). Never earlier than the month after the plan's `effective_from`, since everything bills in arrears. Null for manual or inactive plans.

missing_scopes.description:
The scopes required by this resource and method that the provider did not confirm as
granted.

Present only when both halves of that comparison are known: the provider echoed the
scopes it granted, **and** this resource and method declares required scopes. It is
**absent** — not empty — otherwise, which includes `api_key` and OAuth1 connections
(no scope grant exists), OAuth2 and `jwt_bearer` connections where the provider
omits `scope` from its token response, resources and methods that declare no
required scopes, and requirements that are not OAuth scopes at all
(`refusal_basis: non_scope_requirement` — see `permission_vocabulary`), where no
diff is run and `required_permissions` carries the answer instead.

An empty array therefore means "no *all-of* scope is missing", while an absent
field means "cannot be determined" — two different statements. Read `refusal_basis`
for the one question this field cannot answer on its own, "was anything missing at
all": an empty array sits beside a populated `missing_any_of_scopes` whenever the
whole shortfall is an unmet any-of requirement, so on
`refusal_basis: scopes_missing` an empty array does **not** mean every permission
was granted. It means that on `refusal_basis: scopes_satisfied`, and only there. Do
not default an absent `missing_scopes` to `[]` either: that reads back as "nothing
is missing" about a request that was refused.

Truto's comparison is an inference over integration configuration. The provider's
own account of the refusal is the authoritative one, and Truto relays it without
interpreting it: `raw_response` (the error body verbatim) and `message` (its human
text) on the 403 itself, and a capped copy of the body on this record as
`raw_response_excerpt`. `message` is not persisted, so re-run the call to see it.

Truto deliberately does not lift a "code" or a "documentation link" out of that
body. Which key in an arbitrary provider's error shape is the important one has no
correct general answer, and a confidently wrong one placed above a correct body is
the same failure as reporting a scope missing that was never checked.

refusal_basis.description:
Which of the states below produced this record, so a reader never has to infer it
from the presence or emptiness of `missing_scopes`. Absent on rows recorded before
Truto stored it — and on such a row an empty `missing_scopes` cannot be read as
"compared, nothing missing", because it was also written when nothing had been
compared at all.

**An open set, and `x-extensible-enum` rather than `enum` says so to a code
generator as well as to a reader.** Prose asking for a default branch is not
something a generator reads, and a closed union here can be violated by design:
the read path deliberately accepts an unrecognised value so a row written by a
newer build stays readable after a rollback, and the older build then serves that
value straight back on this field. The values below are what Truto writes today.
Keep a default branch.

The live `truto_error_insight.forbidden_error.value.refusal_basis` keeps a closed
`enum`, and the asymmetry is the point: a running build always emits its own
documented set, while a stored row can carry a value the build reading it never
wrote.

description.description: The sentence the live 403 carried, recorded so this row reads the same as the call did.
description.example: Access forbidden. This operation requires a role or privilege granted in the provider's own admin console, not an OAuth scope — reconnecting will not change it.

missing_any_of_scopes.description:
Scopes of which the operation needs *any one*, where the grant holds none. Kept
apart from `missing_scopes` so alternatives are never reported as though all were
required.

required_permissions.description:
What this operation requires, whether or not a comparison was possible. Always
paired with `permission_vocabulary`, since the same string means "reconnect and
grant this", "add this to your API key" or "ask an admin for this role" depending
on which vocabulary it is written in.

required_any_of_permissions.description: Permissions of which the operation needs *any one*, kept apart from `required_permissions` for the same reason.

permission_vocabulary.description:
Which vocabulary `required_permissions` is written in, and therefore what the
remedy is. Only `oauth_scope` is fixed by reconnecting: `api_key_permission` is
granted to the API key in the provider, and `role_label` in the provider's own
admin console.

`x-extensible-enum` for the same reason as `refusal_basis` above: this is a stored
value, and a rollback can serve one written by a build that knew a fourth
vocabulary. Keep a default branch.

raw_response_excerpt.description:
A capped copy of the integration's own error body, so this record shows what the
provider said and not only what Truto inferred about it. Truncated with a trailing
`… truncated` marker past 2,048 **bytes** of UTF-8, because this record is
deserialized on every proxy and unified call that resolves the account and that cost
is what the bound exists to control. Bytes, not characters: 2,048 characters of CJK
is about 6 KB stored, so a character bound would charge one language three times
what it charges another. Expect fewer characters than 2,048 for any non-ASCII body.
The 2,048 covers the marker as well, so the stored value never exceeds it.

**A truncated excerpt is not parseable.** It is a byte prefix of a serialized body
with a marker on the end, so `JSON.parse` on this field throws whenever truncation
happened — which the trailing `… truncated` is how you detect. Render it as text.
An untruncated excerpt of a JSON body does parse, but nothing guarantees this field
is JSON at all: a plain-text or HTML error body is stored exactly as it arrived.

Absent when the refusal carried no body. Not forwarded to the connections widget:
it is a raw provider string, which is what `connections.show_error_details` exists
to keep away from an end user.

Note that "every remote 403 carries an insight" and "every remote 403 leaves a
record here" are different statements. A Proxy API **custom method** and a **Custom
API** both carry the live insight, but a Custom API names no resource or method, and
writing `{resource: "", method: ""}` would replace a record naming a real call with
one naming none — so no record is written for those. Read the insight on the
response for them.

IntegrationGeneratedField.description:
A single value Truto generates once per connection, declared in a credential's `config.generated_fields` array. Used where the provider requires the value to be produced by Truto rather than by the customer. It is generated for the connection and kept for its life — a reconnect never regenerates it, and a caller-supplied value for the same name is ignored.

- `uuid` — a public value such as an AWS IAM role's External ID, which pins the customer's role trust policy to Truto. Written to the top level of the integrated-account context under `name` and read from placeholders as `{{<name>}}`, exactly like a `config.fields` entry. It is not a credential and is not redacted.
- `rsa_key_pair` — Truto makes an RSA key pair for the connection. Only the **public** half is stored under `name` — `{ public_key, public_key_pem, fingerprint, key_id, key_id_short, created_at }` — and shown to the customer to install in the provider. The **private** half is a credential: it is encrypted, never returned by any API, and never visible to placeholders, mappings or expressions; only a `jwt_bearer` credential that names it in `signing.generated` can sign with it. It cannot be declared on a credential that connects through a browser redirect, or in an integrated account's own `integration_override`.

`name` must be letters, digits and underscores, must not start with `truto_`, and must not be a key Truto stores a secret under (`api_key`, `token`, `oauth`, `secret`, `generated_secrets`, …).

An environment override that sets `generated_fields` replaces the integration's list rather than adding to it, like every other array in an override, so it has to repeat any key pair the integration declares. Truto refuses an override that would leave `signing.generated` naming a key pair the credential no longer declares.

IntegrationAwsStsCredential.description:
AWS STS credential exchange. A long-lived AWS key signs one `AssumeRole` call and AWS returns a short-lived key belonging to whichever account owns the role.

AWS scopes a key to exactly one account, so this is how a connection reads an account its own key does not belong to. Set `token_key` to a per-request template and one connection keeps one cached credential per key, which lets a single connection read a whole AWS Organization.

signing.description:
The IAM key that signs the `AssumeRole` call — a bring-your-own-credential pair on the same footing as an OAuth app's `client.id` / `client.secret`.

Configure it here and every connection uses Truto's key. Leave it out, or set the id to `dummy` or a `{{...}}` template, and the integration reports `requires_oauth_app_setup` until the customer supplies their own on the environment integration `override`, which is merged over this config. The values are read literally — a credential is a value, not a template.

token_key.description:
Which cached credential slot this request uses, as a template resolved against the request context — for example `{{query.truto_account_id}}`.

Omit it, or leave it unresolved on a request that names no account, and the connection uses one shared slot like every other credential format. Set it and each resolved key gets its own slot under `context.oauth.tokens`, refreshed independently.

When `AssumeRole` fails for one slot because of its role (`AccessDenied`, `NoSuchEntity`, …), the connection stays `active` and the failure is recorded under `context.oauth.token_errors.<key>` as `code`, `message`, `first_failed_at` and `last_failed_at`. The entry is cleared when that slot next refreshes.

ignore_limit_in_pagination.description: Don't re-send `limit_key` after the first page (for APIs that reject it on subsequent calls).

use_content_hash.description: Detect loops by hashing each page's results. Only effective when `cursor_path_object` is `body`.

add_to_query.description: Add the cursor to the query string.

is_cursor_url_encoded.description: URL-decode the cursor before sending (some upstreams double-encode).

allow_empty_page_cursor.description: Don't treat an empty cursor as the end of pagination.

IntegrationLinkHeaderPagination.description: RFC 5988 `Link:` header pagination (e.g. GitHub-style). The `next` and `prev` URLs are extracted from the response `Link` header.

page_key.description: Informational only; the actual cursor comes from the `Link` header.

limit_key.description: Query key that holds the page size when the caller sets `limit`.

max_limit.description: Maximum page size Truto will request.

headers.description: Static or templated headers added to every paginated request.

ignore_limit.description: Don't send `limit_key` even when the caller sets `limit`.

total_path.description: Optional dotted-path accessor into the response body that yields the total result count, used to stop paginating early.

offset_key.description: Query/body key that holds the offset.

limit_key.description: Query/body key that holds the page size.

max_limit.description: Maximum page size Truto will request.

headers.description: Static or templated headers added to every paginated request.

add_to_body.description: Send pagination params in the request body instead of the query string.

default_offset.description: Offset used for the first request (some APIs are 1-indexed).

add_to_query.description: Send pagination params in the query string.

use_content_hash.description: Detect loops by hashing each page's results.

ignore_limit.description: Drop `limit_key` from the URL after pagination is applied.

total_path.description: Optional dotted-path accessor into the response body that yields the total result count, used to stop paginating early.

start_key.description: Query/body key that holds the start of the range.

end_key.description: Query/body key that holds the end of the range (exclusive).

max_limit.description: Maximum range size Truto will request.

headers.description: Static or templated headers added to every paginated request.

add_to_body.description: Send pagination params in the request body instead of the query string.

add_to_query.description: Send pagination params in the query string.

default_start.description: Start value used for the first request.

ignore_limit.description: Drop `start_key`, `end_key`, and `limit` from the URL after pagination is applied.

IntegrationDynamicPagination.description: Dynamic pagination driven entirely by JSONata expressions. Use this when none of the canonical strategies fit (e.g. SOAP-style request envelopes, HATEOAS links inside body fields, multi-step resumption tokens).

get_initial_pagination_values_expression.description:
Optional JSONata expression evaluated **before** the first request. Use to seed pagination values (e.g. compute a default `since` window).

Input: `IntegrationDynamicPaginationRequestContext`. Output: `IntegrationDynamicPaginationRequestResult`.

get_pagination_values_expression.description:
JSONata expression evaluated **before each subsequent request** (when `query.next_cursor` is set). Mutates the URL/body/headers/query for the next page.

Input: `IntegrationDynamicPaginationRequestContext` with `query.next_cursor` decoded from base64. Output: `IntegrationDynamicPaginationRequestResult`.

get_cursor_from_response_expression.description:
JSONata expression evaluated **after each response**. Returns the next cursor (Truto then base64-encodes it) and optional loop-detection flags.

Input: `IntegrationDynamicPaginationResponseContext`. Output: `IntegrationDynamicPaginationResponseResult`.

IntegrationAuthorization.description:
How Truto applies the resolved credential to outbound HTTP requests. The `format` discriminator selects which `config` shape applies.

All string values support Truto placeholders (`{{path}}`) resolved against the runtime context. Common placeholder roots: `{{api_key}}` for fields collected at connect time, `{{oauth.token.access_token}}` for OAuth2 access tokens, `{{environment_variables.MY_KEY}}` for env-vars set at the environment-integration level.

value.description: The bearer token. Almost always a placeholder like `{{oauth.token.access_token}}` (OAuth2) or `{{api_key}}` (api-key fields).

IntegrationBasicAuthorization.description: Adds an HTTP Basic `Authorization: Basic base64(username:password)` header.

username.description: Username, supports placeholders (e.g. `{{api_key}}` for vendors that pass the API key as the username).

IntegrationHeaderAuthorization.description: Adds arbitrary headers to every request. Provide either `headers` (static map) or `expression` (JSONata returning the request to send), but not both.

headers.description: Map of header name → value. Values support placeholders (e.g. `{ "X-API-Key": "{{api_key}}" }`).

expression.description:
JSONata expression that fully constructs the outgoing request. Use for advanced cases (request signing, dynamic URL rewrites).

Input: `IntegrationHeaderAuthorizationContext`. Output: `IntegrationHeaderAuthorizationResult` (must contain `url` and `requestOptions`).

IntegrationRateLimit.description: How Truto detects and reacts to upstream rate-limiting. All fields are JSONata expressions evaluated against the upstream response.

is_rate_limited.description:
JSONata expression returning a truthy value when the response should be treated as rate-limited. When omitted, Truto falls back to `status === 429`.

Input: `IntegrationRateLimitExpressionContext`. Output: boolean.

retry_after_header_expression.description:
JSONata expression returning the seconds to wait before retrying. When omitted, Truto reads the standard `Retry-After` header.

Input: `IntegrationRateLimitExpressionContext`. Output: number (seconds).

rate_limit_header_expression.description:
JSONata expression returning the current rate-limit window state. Truto forwards this as `RateLimit-Limit` / `RateLimit-Remaining` / `RateLimit-Reset` headers in the proxy response.

Input: `IntegrationRateLimitExpressionContext`. Output: `IntegrationRateLimitHeaderValues`.

IntegrationWebhookSignatureVerification.description:
Strategy used to verify an inbound webhook's signature. The `format` discriminator selects which `config` shape applies.

All string values inside `config` support Truto placeholders resolved against the inbound webhook `IntegrationWebhookPayloadContext` (`{{body.foo}}`, `{{headers.x-signature}}`, `{{raw_body}}`, `{{context.api_key}}`, etc.).

IntegrationWebhookHmacVerification.description: HMAC signature verification. Truto computes `hmac(algorithm, secret, signed_string)` and compares it (constant-time) with `compare_with`.

IntegrationWebhookHmacVerificationConfig.description: HMAC signature verification. Truto computes `hmac(algorithm, secret, signed_string)` and compares it (constant-time) with `compare_with`.

secret.description: Shared HMAC secret. Typically a placeholder like `{{context.webhook_secret}}` or `{{environment_variables.WEBHOOK_SECRET_secret}}`.

string_type.description: Output encoding for the computed digest.

compare_with.description: The signature value from the request to compare against. Usually a placeholder like `{{headers.x-signature}}`.

parts.description: Ordered list of `IntegrationWebhookPayloadContext` field names to concatenate as the signed string (e.g. `["raw_body"]` or `["timestamp", "raw_body"]`). Mutually exclusive with `verification_content`.

verification_content.description: Ordered list of placeholders to concatenate as the signed string (e.g. `["{{headers.x-timestamp}}", ".", "{{raw_body}}"]`). Mutually exclusive with `parts`.

IntegrationWebhookBasicVerificationConfi.description: HTTP Basic signature verification. Truto base64-encodes `username:password` and compares it with the second word of `compare_with` (i.e. `Authorization: Basic <token>`).

IntegrationWebhookBearerVerificationConf.description: Bearer-token signature verification. Truto compares `secret` (constant-time) with the second word of `compare_with` (i.e. `Authorization: Bearer <token>`).

IntegrationWebhookJwtVerificationConfig.description:
JWT signature verification, in one of two modes.

**Shared secret** (set `secret`): Truto verifies that `compare_with` is a valid HS256 JWT signed with `secret`.

**Issuer key set** (set `jwks_uri`): Truto verifies that `compare_with` is a JWT signed with an asymmetric key published at `jwks_uri`, then checks `issuer`, `audience` and the caller's identity. Use this for tokens such as the OIDC token on a Google Pub/Sub push subscription (`jwks_uri: https://www.googleapis.com/oauth2/v3/certs`, `issuer: https://accounts.google.com`). The `issuer`, `audience` and one of `email` or `subject` are all required, because the issuer signs a token for any caller who asks and a valid signature alone does not identify the sender. A block that omits them, uses a non-HTTPS `jwks_uri`, or sets a non-asymmetric `algorithm` is rejected with a 400 when it is saved (on the integration or on an environment-integration override), instead of failing every inbound webhook afterwards.

secret.description: Shared signing secret for HS256. Supports placeholders. Not used when `jwks_uri` is set.

compare_with.description: The JWT to verify, typically a placeholder like `{{headers.authorization}}` or `{{body.token}}`. With `jwks_uri`, an `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` value is accepted as-is.

jwks_uri.description: HTTPS URL of the issuer's JSON Web Key Set. Setting it selects the issuer-key-set mode. Keys are cached for an hour.

algorithm.description: Asymmetric algorithm the token must use (`RS256`, `RS384`, `RS512`, `PS256`, `PS384`, `PS512`, `ES256`, `ES384`, `ES512` or `EdDSA`). Defaults to `RS256`. Used with `jwks_uri` only.

issuer.description: Required `iss` claim, e.g. `https://accounts.google.com`. Used with `jwks_uri` only.

audience.description: Required `aud` claim. Supports placeholders, e.g. `https://api.truto.one/environment-integration-webhook/{{environment_integration_id}}`. Used with `jwks_uri` only.

email.description: Required `email` claim, e.g. the push subscription's service account. The token's `email_verified` must also be true. Used with `jwks_uri` only.

subject.description: Required `sub` claim. Use instead of, or together with, `email`. Used with `jwks_uri` only.

IntegrationWebhookConfig.description: How Truto receives and verifies inbound webhooks for this integration. **Not** to be confused with `WebhookSchema` elsewhere in this spec, which describes Truto's _outbound_ webhook delivered to your application.

signature_verification.description: Strategy used to verify the webhook signature before accepting it. Runs **after** `payload_transform` and **after** `handle_verification` returns `{ type: 'payload' }`.

handle_verification.description:
JSONata expression evaluated on **every** inbound webhook before signature verification. Use to:
  * Respond to handshake pings (return `{ type: 'verify', verification_response: { status_code, body, headers } }`).
  * Surface meta-events that should not fan out (return `{ type: 'meta' }`).
  * Update the integrated account context (return `{ type: 'verify' \| 'payload' \| 'meta', update_context: { ... } }`).
  * Pass through to fan-out (return `{ type: 'payload' }` or omit entirely — defaults to `payload`).

Input: `IntegrationWebhookPayloadContext`. Output: `IntegrationWebhookHandleVerificationResult`.

payload_transform.description:
JSONata expression that transforms the raw inbound payload **before** `handle_verification` and `signature_verification` see it. Use to normalize vendor-specific envelopes (e.g. unwrap a Salesforce `payloads[]` array, decode a base64 body).

Input: `IntegrationWebhookPayloadContext`. Output: `IntegrationWebhookPayloadContext` (the same shape — what you return becomes the new payload).

IntegrationResourceMethodExample.description: Sample request/response payloads used by docs and the Truto MCP for tool descriptions.

response.description: Sample response body (typically pretty-printed JSON, stored as a string).

query.description: Sample query-string params (stored as a string).

body.description: Sample request body (typically pretty-printed JSON, stored as a string).

IntegrationResourceMethod.description:
Definition of a single resource method (e.g. `users.list`) for an integration.

All `headers`/`query`/`body`/`path` string values support Truto placeholders (`{{...}}`) resolved against the runtime request context.

base_url.description: Override the integration-level `base_url` for this single method. Supports placeholders.

method.description: HTTP method. Includes WebDAV/CalDAV verbs (e.g. `propfind`, `report`) for integrations such as Apple/iCloud Calendar.

path.description: URL path appended to `base_url`. Supports placeholders — `{{id}}` for the path parameter (auto URL-encoded), `{{query.foo}}` for caller query params, `{{<field-name>}}` for credential fields, `{{environment_variables.MY_VAR}}` for env-vars, etc.

pagination_path.description: Optional alternate path to call when paginating (e.g. when the first page comes from `/users` but subsequent pages come from a `next_url` field). Supports placeholders.

authorization.description: Override the integration-level `authorization` for this method (e.g. a method that uses a different credential format than the rest of the integration).

headers.description: Static or templated request headers merged with the integration-level `headers`. Values are templated with placeholders; `null` removes the inherited header.

query.description: Static or templated query-string params merged with caller-supplied `query`. Values may be strings, numbers, booleans, arrays, or placeholders. Array serialization is controlled by `query_array_format`.

query_array_format.description: How array values are serialized in the query string. `comma` → `?a=1,2`; `brackets` → `?a[]=1&a[]=2`; `indices` → `?a[0]=1&a[1]=2`; `repeat` → `?a=1&a=2`.

body.description: Static or templated request body for `post`/`put`/`patch` methods. Values may be any JSON type and may include placeholders. Use `$truto_merge` with `:json` to deep-merge an entire object — see placeholder syntax.

query_schema.description: JSON-schema-style declaration of supported query params used by Truto's MCP/tooling. May be a JSONata string for dynamic schemas, or a `JsonSchemaObject`.

body_schema.description: JSON-schema-style declaration of the supported request body used by Truto's MCP/tooling. May be a JSONata string for dynamic schemas, or a `JsonSchemaObject`. The runtime (see `src/mcp/mcpRouter.ts`) reads `body_schema.properties`, so callers should emit the wrapped `JsonSchemaObject` shape `{ type "object", properties { ... } }` rather than a flat `{ name { type "string" } }` map.

body_format.description:
How the request body is serialized:
  * `json` — JSON-encoded (default).
  * `form` — `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`.
  * `multipart` — `multipart/form-data`. See `IntegrationResourceMethodBodyFormatConfigMultipart` for tuning options. The file field is declared in `body_schema` as `type: string, format: binary`.
  * `raw` — sent verbatim, with `Content-Type` set from `body_format_config.content_type`. For a file upload `body_schema` has exactly one property, `file` as `type: string, format: binary`; for a raw text body, a single plain `type: string` property. `raw` is also used to send a structured body under its own content type (for example `application/vnd.api+json` or `application/scim+json`), which is not a file and keeps an ordinary `body_schema`.
  * `xml` — converted to XML and sent as `application/xml`.

body_format_config.description: Extra options for the chosen `body_format`. Discriminated by the sibling `body_format` field — see `IntegrationResourceMethodBodyFormatConfigRaw` (for `raw`) and `IntegrationResourceMethodBodyFormatConfigMultipart` (for `multipart`). Ignored for `json`/`form`/`xml`. `anyOf`, not `oneOf`: the multipart shape has no required keys and no `additionalProperties: false`, so a raw config (`{ content_type }`) also satisfies it and `oneOf` rejected every raw method.

response_schema.description: JSON-schema-style declaration of the response payload used by Truto's MCP/tooling.

response_path.description: Dotted-path accessor (e.g. `data.results`, `payload.users.*`, `result.0.items`) into the parsed response that contains the canonical resource (or array of resources). Defaults to the root. This is a path lookup, **not** a JSONata expression.

pagination.description: Override the integration-level pagination for this single method. Set to `null` to disable pagination on a method that would otherwise inherit it.

add_query_to_body.description: For `post`/`put`/`patch` methods, copy the caller-supplied query params into the body before sending.

ignore_body_in_pagination.description: Don't re-send the body when fetching subsequent pagination pages.

ignore_body.description: Drop the body entirely (useful for vendors that 400 on empty bodies).

set_body_to_null.description: Send a literal JSON `null` instead of an empty body.

no_auth.description: Skip applying the integration's authorization to this method (e.g. a public health check).

ignore_credentials_on_redirect.description: Strip the Authorization header when the upstream issues a redirect to a different host.

throw_error_on_parse_error.description: When true, fail loudly if the response can't be parsed; otherwise return a structured error.

error_expression.description:
JSONata expression evaluated on every response (success or failure). Use to detect errors in successful (2xx) responses, normalize error messages, or transform "errors" with `< 400` status into successful responses with the `result` you return.

Input: `IntegrationErrorExpressionContext`. Output: `IntegrationErrorExpressionResult` — return `null`/`undefined` to indicate "no error", or a `{ status, message?, headers?, metadata?, result? }` object.

description.description: Human-readable description of the method, used in MCP tool listings.

api_documentation_url.description: URL to the upstream vendor's documentation for this method.

scopes.description:
Permissions required to call this method, **all** of which are needed. Usually OAuth
scopes, but an integration that issues no OAuth grant, or whose permissions are role
names, writes those here instead — which vocabulary is in use is derived from the
integration, or declared here with `permission_vocabulary`.

scopes_any_of.description:
Permissions of which holding **any one** is enough, kept apart from `scopes` (which is
all-of). Providers say so explicitly — Microsoft Graph answers a 403 with "API requires
one of 'Chat.ReadBasic.All, Chat.Read.All, Chat.ReadWrite.All'" — and treating that as
all-of reports scopes as missing that the operation never needed.

permission_vocabulary.description:
Which vocabulary `scopes` and `scopes_any_of` above are written in, declared rather
than inferred. Normally omitted: Truto derives this from configuration that already
exists, so every integration is classified without anyone labelling it. Set it only to
correct a derivation that reads an integration wrongly.

It exists because the derivation is deliberately whole-integration — an author writes
one list in one vocabulary throughout, and only some entries carry the proof — which
makes it correct for every integration in production and unable to express an
exception. `jamf` is the exception: nine methods declare console role labels
(`Read - Users`) and `users.create` declares a real OAuth scope (`users:create`), and
no integration-wide answer is right for both. Declaring it on the one method leaves the
other eighty untouched.

An unrecognised value falls back to the derivation rather than being reported to a
customer.

mcp_annotations.description:
Hints mirroring MCP `ToolAnnotations` for this method's tool, read by consumers that
classify tools (e.g. Elaichi) to decide read, write or destructive. Keys keep the MCP
spec's camelCase spelling on purpose. Absent means "no hint": consumers fall back to
their existing rules, and a missing flag is not read as `false`. `readOnlyHint` and
`destructiveHint` cannot both be `true`.

readOnlyHint.description: The tool does not modify its environment.

destructiveHint.description: The tool may perform destructive updates (as opposed to purely additive ones).

idempotentHint.description: Calling the tool repeatedly with the same arguments has no additional effect.

openWorldHint.description: The tool interacts with an open world of external entities (as opposed to a closed domain).

before.description:
Steps to run before this method's own request: an array of steps run in order, or a
string naming a sibling method whose steps are reused. Same step shape as a unified
model mapping's `before`. Accepted and stored so engines that run proxy configs can
execute it; **Truto's own proxy does not run it yet**, so on Truto this is inert.
Each step's `run_if` must parse as JSONata, or the write is a 400.

IntegrationResourceMethodBodyFormatConfi.description: `body_format_config` shape when `body_format` is `raw`. The body is sent verbatim with the configured `content_type`.

content_type.description: `Content-Type` header to attach to the raw body.

IntegrationResourceMethodBodyFormatConfi.description: `body_format_config` shape when `body_format` is `multipart`. Tunes how nested JSON values are serialized into multipart fields.

showLeafArrayIndexes.description: When true (the default), indexed leaf arrays are serialized as `field[0]=a&field[1]=b`; when false, as `field[]=a&field[]=b`.

includeNullValues.description: When true, `null` values are sent as the literal string `"null"`. Defaults to `false` (omitted).

mapping.description: Optional pre-serialization value mapper. Keyed by JSON type; each value is a function that returns a string. Rarely needed.

IntegrationActionStep.description: A single step in an integration `action` (post-install hook, validation hook, refresh-token override, custom flows). Steps run sequentially with a shared `context`.

type.description:
Step kind:
  * `request` — perform an HTTP call (config matches `IntegrationResourceMethod`).
  * `transform` — apply a JSONata expression over the running context.
  * `update_context` / `set_context` — write into the shared step context.
  * `get_context` — read from the shared step context.
  * `form` — pause and ask the connected user to fill a form (post-connect form).

config.description: Step-specific configuration. For `request`, accepts the same shape as `IntegrationResourceMethod`. For `transform`, a JSONata expression string. For `form`, a fields array.

IntegrationAction.description: A named integration action. Built-in actions are `post_install`, `post_connect_user_form`, `refresh_token`, and `validation`; arbitrary names are also allowed for custom flows triggered via the proxy or sync runtime.

steps.description: Ordered list of steps to run when the action is invoked.

type.description: Optional action type tag (e.g. `request` for single-shot actions). When omitted, `steps` is used.

config.description: Optional top-level config used when `type` is set instead of `steps`.

IntegrationConfig.description: Complete integration configuration. Validated by Truto on `POST /integration` and `PATCH /integration/{id}`.

base_url.description: Default base URL prepended to every resource method's `path`.

label.description: Human-readable name shown in the Truto Dashboard and Link UI.

logo.description: URL to the integration logo (square, recommended 256x256).

icon.description: URL to a smaller monochrome icon used in catalog listings.

headers.description: Default HTTP headers merged into every outbound request. Values may be templated with JSONata placeholders.

query.description: Default query-string params merged into every outbound request.

actions.description: Named integration actions. Reserved keys (`post_install`, `post_connect_user_form`, `refresh_token`, `validation`) hook into specific platform lifecycle events; custom names are callable from the proxy/sync runtime.

credentials.description: Either a single credential definition (when the integration only supports one auth format) or a map keyed by auth format (when an integration supports multiple, e.g. `api_key` and `oauth2`). For multi-format integrations, the customer picks one in the Connect UI. Each credential's `config.label` and `config.help_text` customize the auth-method card shown in the Connect UI.

resources.description: Resource → method tree (e.g. `resources.users.list`). The inner key is one of the canonical methods (`list`, `get`, `create`, `update`, `delete`) or a custom method name. Each method definition matches `IntegrationResourceMethod`.

tool_tags.description:
Optional tag arrays keyed by resource name (`contacts`) or
`resource.method` (`contacts.delete`). Method-level tags are unioned
with resource-level tags when building MCP tools and filtering by
MCP token `config.tags`.

error_expression.description:
Integration-wide JSONata expression evaluated on every response. Use to detect errors in successful (2xx) responses, normalize error messages, or transform "errors" with `< 400` status into successful responses. Overridden by per-method `IntegrationResourceMethod.error_expression` when set.

Input: `IntegrationErrorExpressionContext`. Output: `IntegrationErrorExpressionResult` — return `null`/`undefined` to indicate "no error", or a `{ status, message?, headers?, metadata?, result? }` object.

browser_file_picker_requires_access_toke.description:
This provider's **browser** file picker cannot run without the connected account's upstream `access_token`, so `GET /integrated-account/me` releases `context.oauth.token.access_token` — and nothing else — to a connect-flow integrated account token. Google Drive and Box need it; their picker SDKs take the token client-side. SharePoint, OneDrive and Dropbox authenticate by other means and must leave this unset.

A `refresh_token` is never released, whatever this is set to. Honoured only on the integration's own `config`: it is not part of `EnvironmentIntegrationConfig`, and it is stripped from an integrated account's `integration_override`, so it cannot be switched on for a single environment or account.

oauth_app_headers.description:
Headers built from the connected account's OAuth app and sent on every request, for providers that want the app's own key next to the user's token. Etsy, for example, needs `{ "x-api-key": "{{client.id}}:{{client.secret}}" }`.

A value may use `{{client.id}}` and `{{client.secret}}` — the OAuth client the account's token was issued to, read and filled in as the token refresh does — and no other placeholder. Saving an integration fails with a 400 if a value uses any other placeholder, or if a header name is one that debug output echoes back (`x-truto-*`, `content-type`, `accept`, `user-agent` and similar).

A header that can't be filled completely is left out: a client field it uses is unset, or is still a placeholder the account's context can't fill. Added after `authorization`, replacing a header of the same name in any letter case. Only accounts connected with `oauth2` get these headers, and a method with `no_auth` doesn't.

Honoured only on the integration's own `config`: it is not part of `EnvironmentIntegrationConfig`, and it is stripped from an integrated account's `integration_override`.

A header that uses `{{client.secret}}` is sent only to the sites of the requests configured by whoever set that secret: the integration, or an environment's override over it. An environment or account override that keeps that app but sends requests elsewhere (its own `base_url`, a method's URL, an `authorization` expression, a mapping's path) sends them without these headers. Through a Static Gate, the target URL counts. An account's own secret (in its `integration_override`, or filled in from its context) goes wherever its requests go.

EnvironmentIntegrationCredentialOverride.description: Per-environment credential override. Either a full credential definition (BYOA: customer supplies their own OAuth client) or `{ enabled: false }` to disable a credential format that the base integration ships with.

enabled.description: Set to `false` to hide this credential format from the Connect UI in this environment.

EnvironmentIntegrationResourceMethod.description: Per-environment override for a single resource method. Same shape as `IntegrationResourceMethod` but every field is optional (deep-merged on top of the base method). `path` is also optional here.

headers.description: Override or add request headers for this method. Values may include JSONata placeholders.

query.description: Override or add query params for this method. Values may include JSONata placeholders.

body.description: Override the request body for this method. Values may include JSONata placeholders.

query_schema.description: Override the query schema. May be a JSONata string or a `JsonSchemaObject`.

body_schema.description: Override the body schema. May be a JSONata string or a `JsonSchemaObject`. See `IntegrationResourceMethod.body_schema` for shape rationale.

scopes_any_of.description:
Per-environment override for the any-of half of the requirement. See
`IntegrationResourceMethod.scopes_any_of`.

permission_vocabulary.description:
Per-environment override for which vocabulary `scopes` and `scopes_any_of` are written
in. See `IntegrationResourceMethod.permission_vocabulary` for what the values mean and
why the field normally stays unset. Overriding it here corrects one environment without
touching the base integration.

mcp_annotations.description:
Per-environment override for the method's MCP `ToolAnnotations` hints. See
`IntegrationResourceMethod.mcp_annotations`. Absent means "no hint". Hints merge per
key with the base method, so to tighten a base read to destructive the override must
also set `readOnlyHint: false`; a merged object with both `true` is treated as no hint.

readOnlyHint.description: The tool does not modify its environment.

destructiveHint.description: The tool may perform destructive updates (as opposed to purely additive ones).

idempotentHint.description: Calling the tool repeatedly with the same arguments has no additional effect.

openWorldHint.description: The tool interacts with an open world of external entities (as opposed to a closed domain).

before.description:
Per-environment override for the method's `before` steps. See
`IntegrationResourceMethod.before`. Arrays are replaced wholesale, not merged per
step, so an override of `[]` clears the base method's `before` for this environment.
Stored only; Truto's own proxy does not run it yet.

EnvironmentIntegrationConfig.description:
Per-environment configuration override for an integration. Stored on `environment_integration.override` and **deep-merged** on top of the base `integration.config` at request time.

Customers most often use this to:
  * Override `webhook.handle_verification` / `webhook.payload_transform`.
  * Override `pagination` or `rate_limit` for a misbehaving vendor instance.
  * Override `authorization` (e.g. add a custom header).
  * Provide BYOA OAuth client IDs/secrets via `credentials.<format>`.
  * Override Connect UI copy per auth method via `credentials.<format>.config.label` and `credentials.<format>.config.help_text`.

description.description: Environment-specific description shown in the catalog.

tags.description: Environment-specific tags shown in the catalog.

is_beta.description: Environment-specific beta flag shown in the catalog and Connect UI. Deep-merged onto `integration.is_beta` at request time.

environment_variables.description: Free-form key/value pairs available to JSONata as `{{env.<key>}}` for this integration in this environment. Values can be of any type (string, number, boolean, object, array).

JsonSchemaObjectProperties.description: A single property entry in a JSON Schema-style declaration. Used for `query_schema`, `body_schema`, `request_body_schema`, and the inner `properties` map of `JsonSchemaObject`.

$ref.description: JSON Schema `$ref` pointer (used when this property references another schema).

required.description: Whether this property is required. Truto uses a boolean per-property convention rather than the standard JSON Schema `required` array.

items.description: When `type=array`, the element schema (only `type` is enforced).

mapping.description: JSONata expression (string) or an object-form mapping describing how to project this property out of the integration response.

default.description: Default value used when the caller omits this field.

format.description: Optional format hint (e.g. `date-time`, `uuid`). On a `body_schema` property, `type: string` + `format: binary` declares FILE BYTES. The rule, exactly: the property is TOP-LEVEL (or the `items` of a top-level array of files, `multipart` only; Elaichi does not send multipart arrays as files yet, which needs `noSquareBrackets: true` on the method and cardamom#30, so a single file field works today and the lint warns on an array) and is `type: string` (an untyped `{format: binary}` is not a file), and the method's effective body is `multipart` (a file part named after the property) or `raw` (the ONE property of the body, under a content type that is not a data format; an array of files is not read under `raw`). The effective body is the engine's: an unset `body_format` means `json` for a `list` method and a DELETE `delete`, and NO body for every other method, and `multipart` on list/get/delete or `raw` on get/delete is not built at all. `format: binary` on a `json`/`form`/`xml` body (or a method that sends no body) is not read as a file; a file carried as base64 text in a `json`/`form` body uses `contentEncoding` instead.

contentEncoding.description: JSON Schema `contentEncoding`. On a TOP-LEVEL `type: string` property (or the `items` of a top-level array) of a `json` or `form` `body_schema`, `base64` / `base64url` (case-insensitive) declares that the string carries a file's content encoded as text (for example Microsoft Graph `contentBytes`). Elaichi reads it in `json` and `form` bodies and also as a scalar part in `multipart`; it is not read in `raw` (the body is the bytes, declared with `format: binary`) or `xml`, and a multipart ARRAY of encoded parts is deferred like an array of files. `format: byte` alone is not a file. Never combine it with `format: binary`.

conditionallyRequiredDescription.description: Free-form description shown when the property is required only in certain contexts.

xTrutoReference.description: Truto-specific cross-resource reference metadata. Either a single reference object, an array of references, or omitted entirely. Explicit `null` is also accepted to clear any inherited reference.

body_field.description: Body field on the unified call used to discriminate between fragments.

config.description: Strategy-specific options (e.g. multipart field name, base64 wrapper key).

user_role.description: List of vendor user roles required for this integration mapping to work.

scopes.description: OAuth/API key scopes required for this integration mapping.

static.description: Static value returned for this method without making an HTTP call.

resource.description: Integration resource to call. May be a single name, an array of resource fragments, or a `{ expression, resources }` object for dynamic dispatch.

response_mapping.description: JSONata expression (string) or object-form mapping. The object form is keyed by field name with values that may be JSONata strings, nested objects, or `JsonSchemaObjectProperties`.

request_body_schema.description: Object-form (v2) request body schema; values are partial JSON Schema entries.

query.description: Static query params merged into the integration request.

body.description: Static body merged into the integration request.

oneOf.description: Free-form method names → mapping (for custom unified methods).

deprecated.description: When true, marks the method as deprecated in docs/tools.

environment_unified_model_id.description: The `environment_unified_model` record (environment + unified model pair) this override belongs to.

persisted.description: Number of records actually written to the destination (datastore, super-query, or webhook).

EnvironmentUnifiedModelMappingStep.description: A single `before` / `after` step. Used by unified-model resource methods, where Truto runs it around the main HTTP request, and by `before` on proxy resource methods (`IntegrationResourceMethod.before`), where Truto only stores it for engines that run proxy configs.

type.description: Step kind. `request` performs an HTTP call against any integration resource; `state`/`replace_data` are reserved for runtime state mutation.

name.description: Optional step identifier referenced from later steps via `{{steps.<name>.response}}`.

run_if.description: JSONata expression; if it evaluates to falsy the step is skipped.

delay_ms.description: Optional fixed delay (in milliseconds) before the step runs.

config.description:
Step-specific config. For `request` on a unified-model method, the same shape as a unified-model integration mapping (`resource`, `method`, `query_mapping`, `body_mapping`, etc.).

On a proxy resource method a `request` step is a proxy call: `{ "type": "proxy", "resource": "conversations", "method": "info", "config": { "query": {...}, "body": {...}, "id": "..." } }`. A missing `type` means a unified call, which an engine that only runs proxy configs does not support. String values in the inner `config` take `{{...}}` placeholders. A `state` step takes `{ "expression": "<JSONata>" }` and a `replace_data` step takes `{ "name": "<earlier step name>" }`. `run_if` is parsed as JSONata on write.

EnvironmentUnifiedModelSideLoad.description: Side-load configuration that fetches related records and merges them into the response under `path`.

path.description: JSON path inside the unified response where the side-loaded data should be attached.

response_mapping.description: JSONata expression that produces the side-loaded value from the related record.

EnvironmentUnifiedModelResourceMethodOve.description:
Per-environment override for a single unified-model resource method (e.g. `crm.contacts.list` on `salesforce`).

All fields are optional and **field-replaced** on top of the base method (the deep-merge does not recurse into individual mapping objects — supplying `response_mapping` replaces the base `response_mapping` entirely).

static.description: Static value returned for this method without making an HTTP call. Useful for stubbing.

resource.description: Override which integration resource this method points to. Either a resource name, an array of resource fragments to merge, or `{ expression, resources }` to pick dynamically.

method.description: Override which integration method this maps to.

base_url_mapping.description: JSONata expression returning a per-call base URL override.

path_mapping.description: JSONata expression returning a per-call path override.

error_mapping.description: JSONata expression returning an error message when the upstream response should be treated as an error.

mapping_version.description: Mapping schema version. `2` opts into object-form mappings (`*_schema` fields); omit (`undefined`) for legacy string-form mappings (`*_mapping` fields).

response_mapping_method.description: For object-form mappings, whether the response represents a single item or an array.

response_mapping.description: JSONata expression (string) or object-form mapping that transforms the integration response into the unified-model shape.

related_resources.description: Sub-fetches that run after the main request to enrich the response. Either a JSONata string or an array of related-resource configs.

request_body_schema.description: Object-form (v2) request body schema (JSON-schema-style with embedded mappings).

request_body_mapping.description: Legacy (v1) string-form request body mapping, OR object-form (v2) request body mapping.

query_mapping.description: Legacy (v1) string-form query mapping, OR object-form (v2) query mapping.

request_header_mapping.description: JSONata expression that transforms the unified-API request headers before sending.

response_header_mapping.description: JSONata expression that transforms the integration response headers before returning.

query.description: Static query params merged into the integration request. Values may be templated JSONata expressions.

body.description: Static body merged into the integration request. Values may be templated JSONata expressions.

before.description: Pre-request steps. Either a JSONata string for inline transforms or an array of `EnvironmentUnifiedModelMappingStep`.

is_partial_response.description: Marks the response as partial; downstream sync engines will treat missing fields as "unknown" rather than "deleted".

is_partial_expression.description: JSONata expression that returns true when the response should be considered partial.

file_upload.description: File-upload strategy for `create`/`update` methods that accept files.

EnvironmentUnifiedModelResourceOverride.description: Per-environment override for a single unified-model resource (e.g. `contacts` in the `crm` model).

schema.description: Partial JSON schema for the resource. Field-merged on top of the base resource schema.

EnvironmentUnifiedModelOverride.description:
Per-environment override for a unified-model installation. Stored on `environment_unified_model.override` and deep-merged on top of the base `unified_model`.

For per-method JSONata mapping overrides (the most common customization), prefer the dedicated `environment-unified-model-resource-method` resource; this `override` shape is for resource-level overrides (schema, integration_mapping table, scopes, webhooks, docs).

resources.description:
Resource-level overrides keyed by resource name.

A `null` value is a tombstone: it removes an inherited resource from this environment's effective unified model. Omitting the key cannot say that — overrides are deep-merged, so an absent key means "inherit from the base model". The tombstone is stripped while merging, so the resource is simply absent from the returned `unified_model` rather than present with a null value.

additionalProperties.description: Overrides for this resource, or `null` to remove the inherited resource from this environment.

scopes.description: Per-integration extra OAuth scopes appended to the base unified-model scopes.

webhooks.description: Per-integration JSONata expressions that route inbound webhooks to unified-model resources.

UnifiedApiMetaResponse.description: Response from `GET /unified/{model_name}/{resource_name}/{integration_name}/meta/{method}`. Returns the merged JSON schema, default query/body, and documentation link for a single integration mapping. Useful for inspecting what a unified call will accept and return without touching a real integrated account.

method.description: The unified method this metadata describes.

documentation_link.description: Vendor documentation URL for this method, if set on the integration mapping.

response_schema.description: A subset of `schema` containing only the fields actually populated by `response_mapping` for this integration.

query_schema.description: JSON-schema-style description of the supported query parameters for this method.

request_body_schema.description: JSON-schema-style description of the supported request body for this method.

default_query.description: Default query parameters always applied by the integration mapping. Values may be templated JSONata expressions.

default_body.description: Default request body always applied by the integration mapping. Values may be templated JSONata expressions. Object or `null` (arrays are allowed at runtime but rare).

resource.description: The name of the resource to sync. For Unified APIs, it should be in the format `unified_api_name/resource_name`. For Proxy API, it can just be `resource_name`.
resource.example: For fetching Contacts from CRM Unified API, `crm/contacts`. For fetching Contacts from a Proxy API, `contacts`.

method.description: The method to call on the resource.

id.description: The ID of the resource to sync. This is optional and can be used to sync a single resource. It also supports placeholders.
id.example: Static value like `4a4de828-f4db-4c9e-adfd-434e0864c3c7` or placeholder like `{{args.user_id}}`.

query.description: The query parameters to pass to the resource method. It supports placeholders for values.

loop_on.description: When a particular placeholder argument is an array and you want to repeat the request for each element in that array, you can set this parameter. For example, if you accept an argument called `user_ids` which is an array of strings, and you want to fetch each user's details, you can set this parameter to `user_ids` and the request will be repeated for each element in the `user_ids` array.

depends_on.description: The resource that this resource depends on (parent resource). This is optional and can be used to sync a resource only after another resource has been synced. Each object synced for the parent resource is available as the resources object in placeholders for the child resource, e.g. `{{resources.crm.contacts.id}}` if depends on is `crm/contacts` resource.

persist.description: Whether to persist the resource in the database or not in case of a Daemon sync job run or send as a payload in case of RapidBridge sync job run. The Proxy API resources are by default NOT persisted and this parameter can be set to `true` to persist them. Unified API resources are always persisted.

daemon_id.description: The daemon_id attribute of a daemon that is running this sync job.

daemon_group_key.description: The name of the daemon group that this sync job run should be assigned to. Used while creating a sync job run. Truto find a daemon in the group that is available to run the sync job. You can either specify `daemon_group_key` (Daemon) or `webhook_id` (RapidBridge), but NOT both while creating a Sync Job Run.

In case of `ignore`, you'll receive `sync_job_run:record_error` events for each error encountered. In case of `batch`, you'll receive `sync_job_run:record_error` events with multiple errors batched into the errors array, this is only supported when the `version` used for Sync Job Run is 2.

resource_stats.description: The statistics of the resources synced in the sync job run. This will have information around how many records were fetched and persisted by the sync job run -- grouped by the resource and method. The data is updated every 10 seconds while the sync job run is running.
