updated_at.description: The date and time when the sync job run was last updated.

started_at.description: The date and time when the sync job run was started.

finished_at.description: The date and time when the sync job run was finished.

sync_job.description: The sync job that this sync job run belongs to.

integrated_account_id.description: The ID of the integrated account that this sync job cron trigger should run.

daemon_group_key.description: The name of the daemon group that this sync job run should be assigned to. Used while creating a sync job run. Truto find a daemon in the group that is available to run the sync job. You can either specify `daemon_group_key` (Daemon) or `webhook_id` (RapidBridge), but NOT both while creating a Sync Job Run.

created_at.description: The date and time when the sync job run was created.

updated_at.description: The date and time when the sync job run was last updated.

Documentation row type. Per-method MCP tooling uses `description`, `tool_name`, `query_schema`,
`body_schema`, and `response_schema`. Integration-wide rows include `readme`, `oauth_*`, and `note`.

Row payload. For `tool_name`, a snake_case MCP tool name override (max 64 chars, `[a-z0-9_]`).
For `description`, plain text. For `*_schema` types, YAML-encoded schema.

IntegrationPlaceholderContext.description:
Runtime request context used to resolve every `{{...}}` placeholder in an integration config (`headers`, `query`, `body`, `path`, etc.) and to seed every `update_context` action step. Built per request from the integrated-account context plus the current call's parameters.

Lookups use a dotted-path syntax — `{{a.b.c}}`, `{{list.0.id}}`, `{{nested.*.email}}`, etc. — with optional type-casts and fallbacks.

> Top-level fields from the integrated-account context (including credential `fields` collected via the Link form) are spread directly onto this object, so an `IntegrationField` named `subdomain` is read as `{{subdomain}}`.

token.description: OAuth token bag merged from the most recent token-refresh response.

environment_variables.description: Environment-scoped variables defined under Settings → Environment Variables. Read as `{{environment_variables.<NAME>}}`.

truto_authentication_method.description: The authentication format the integrated account was created with (`api_key`, `oauth2`, `oauth`, `oauth2_client_credentials`, `keka_oauth`, `jwt_bearer`, `aws_sts`). Useful when the same integration supports multiple credential formats.

truto_token_key.description:
The credential slot this request resolved to, on an `aws_sts` connection. An `authorization` expression selects the credential with `$lookup(context.oauth.tokens, context.truto_token_key)`.

Absent when the request named no account — a credential declaring a per-request `token_key` that this request did not fill. The lookup then yields nothing and the request fails, rather than signing with whichever credential happened to be in a shared slot.

Always select the slot with this, never by re-deriving it from `context.query`: a proxy request carries the caller's query whole, while a unified request keeps only `truto_`-prefixed keys, so the two disagree.

truto_static_gate_id.description: When the request is routed via a static-gate environment variable, this holds the gate ID.

IntegrationErrorExpressionContext.description: Input passed to every `error_expression` JSONata expression.

status.description: HTTP status code of the upstream response.

headers.description: Lower-cased response headers from the upstream call.

data.description: Parsed response body. If the body is a plain object with a top-level `data` field, that field is used directly; otherwise the whole parsed body is provided.

response.description: Raw [Fetch `Response`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Response) object. Prefer `headers`, `status`, and `data`; this is exposed for advanced inspection only.

IntegrationErrorExpressionResult.description: Return value from an `error_expression`. Return `null` (or omit) to indicate "no error". Returning an object short-circuits with that error shape. When `status < 400`, the `result` field is bubbled up as a successful response (useful for vendors that signal "no data" via 200 with an error body).

status.description: HTTP-style status code that Truto should report (e.g. `429`, `404`, `503`). Use `< 400` to convert an upstream "error" into a successful response.

message.description: Human-readable error message attached to the resulting Truto error.

headers.description: Optional headers to attach to the resulting error/response.

metadata.description: Optional structured metadata propagated to the dashboard error log and webhook payloads.

result.description: Optional payload returned in lieu of the upstream response when `status < 400` (e.g. when the upstream returns 200 with an error envelope, you can normalize the shape here).

status.description: HTTP status code of the upstream response.

headers.description: Lower-cased response headers from the upstream call.

IntegrationRateLimitHeaderValues.description: Return value from `rate_limit.rate_limit_header_expression`. Truto rewrites these into the standard `ratelimit-limit`, `ratelimit-remaining`, and `ratelimit-reset` response headers.

limit.description: Total requests allowed in the current window.

remaining.description: Requests remaining in the current window.

reset.description: When the current window resets — typically a Unix timestamp or ISO date string, exactly as the upstream returned it.

IntegrationWebhookPayloadContext.description:
Input passed to `webhook.handle_verification`, `webhook.payload_transform`, and the `webhook.signature_verification.config` placeholder resolver.

For `payload_transform` specifically, **whatever object you return becomes the new `payload`** for downstream `signature_verification` and the Truto webhook delivery — so the return shape should match this same schema.

body.description: Parsed JSON body of the inbound webhook request.

raw_body.description: Raw (unparsed) request body. Required for HMAC verification of vendors that sign the exact byte stream.

query_params.description: Query-string params from the webhook callback URL (e.g. Truto's signed handshake parameters).

integrated_account_id.description: The integrated account this webhook was delivered to. Present for per-account webhook URLs.

environment_id.description: The environment ID resolved from the webhook URL.

environment_integration_id.description: The environment-integration ID. Present for environment-level webhook URLs.

webhook_type.description: `verify` for handshake/challenge requests, `payload` for real event deliveries, `meta` for Truto metadata pings.

context.description: The full integrated-account context (credentials, OAuth tokens, env vars, etc.). Same shape as the request context used elsewhere.

IntegrationWebhookHandleVerificationResu.description:
Return value from `webhook.handle_verification`.

Use `type: "verify"` to short-circuit the request with a synchronous response (the typical webhook-handshake / URL-verification pattern). Use `type: "payload"` to continue normal payload processing. Use `type: "meta"` for Truto-emitted metadata responses.

type.description: Branch selector — `verify` returns `verification_response` directly to the vendor; `payload` falls through to normal event handling.

verification_response.description: Used when `type: "verify"`. Truto sends this back as the HTTP response to the vendor's handshake.

body.description: Response body (serialized as JSON unless the headers say otherwise).

update_context.description: Optional patch to merge into the integrated-account context after handling this verification. Useful for storing vendor-issued subscription IDs, signing secrets, etc.

IntegrationDynamicPaginationRequestConte.description:
Input for `pagination.config.get_initial_pagination_values_expression` and `get_pagination_values_expression`.

On subsequent pages, `query.next_cursor` is decoded from base64 before being passed in (i.e. you receive the raw cursor string the previous response yielded).

query.description: Caller-supplied query params (with `next_cursor` already base64-decoded on subsequent pages).

requestOptions.description: Current [Fetch `RequestInit`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/RequestInit) (headers, body, method, etc.). Treat as opaque unless you need to inject vendor-specific options.

IntegrationDynamicPaginationRequestResul.description: Return value from `pagination.config.get_initial_pagination_values_expression` / `get_pagination_values_expression`. All fields are optional; only what you return is applied.

url.description: Replacement request URL for the next page.

query.description: Query params to merge onto the URL (overwrites existing keys).

body.description: Replacement request body for the next page.

requestOptions.description: Patch to deep-merge into the current [Fetch `RequestInit`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/RequestInit). Useful for adding pagination-specific headers.

paginationValues.description: Free-form bag of values Truto echoes back to subsequent expressions (for multi-step cursors that need to remember intermediate state).

url.description: Final request URL that produced this response.

response.description: Raw [Fetch `Response`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Response) object. Headers and status are accessible here when you need to read pagination metadata from headers (e.g. `response.headers`).

body.description: Parsed response body (object or array). Truto skips the expression if the body isn't an object/array.

query.description: Caller-supplied query params for this request.

paginationValues.description: `paginationValues` echoed from the most recent `get_pagination_values_expression` invocation.

IntegrationDynamicPaginationResponseResu.description: Return value from `pagination.config.get_cursor_from_response_expression`. Truto base64-encodes `nextCursor` and `prevCursor` before storing them on the synthetic `query.next_cursor` for the next page.

nextCursor.description: Cursor for the next page. Return `null` to signal "no more pages".

prevCursor.description: Optional cursor for the previous page (for two-way paginators).

isLooping.description: Set to `true` if the response is identical to the previous one and Truto should stop paginating to avoid an infinite loop.

IntegrationHeaderAuthorizationContext.description: Input for `authorization.config.expression` (only used when `authorization.format` is `header` and the integration needs custom URL/body manipulation alongside the auth header).

context.description: Same request context used for placeholder resolution — credentials, OAuth tokens, env vars, etc.

IntegrationHeaderAuthorizationResult.description: Return value from `authorization.config.expression`. Both `url` and `requestOptions` are required; Truto throws "Invalid result from custom header jsonata expression" when either is missing.

url.description: New request URL (string or URL object).

requestOptions.description: New [Fetch `RequestInit`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/RequestInit) (must include any auth headers you want to send).

Passkey.description: A registered WebAuthn credential, sanitized for display. Credential material (`credential_id`, `public_key`) is never returned.

id.description: The unique ID of the passkey. Use this to rename or delete it.

name.description: User-supplied label, or `null` when the passkey was registered without one.

device_type.description: `multiDevice` for a synced passkey (iCloud Keychain, Google Password Manager); `singleDevice` for a device-bound one (a security key, or a platform authenticator that does not sync).

backup_state.description: Whether the credential is currently synced into a backup (the WebAuthn BS flag). Refreshed on every sign-in.

last_used_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of the last successful sign-in with this passkey; `null` if it has never been used.

created_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of registration.

PasskeyRegistrationOptions.description: A bare `PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptionsJSON` — pass it straight to `navigator.credentials.create({ publicKey })`. Serialized by `@simplewebauthn/server`; the fields below are the ones the ceremony depends on.

rp.description: Relying party. `id` is the environment's `APP_URL` host, so a passkey registered on one environment is never offered on another.

user.description: User handle the authenticator groups credentials under. `id` is the base64url-encoded Truto user id.

challenge.description: base64url challenge. Single-use, stored server-side for 5 minutes.

excludeCredentials.description: The user's existing credentials, so an authenticator they already enrolled refuses to register a duplicate.

authenticatorSelection.description: `residentKey: required` because sign-in is usernameless, and `userVerification: required` so every assertion carries a second factor — which is what lets a passkey login satisfy `mfa_required`.

extensions.description: Client extensions the library asks for. `credProps` lets the browser report back whether the credential really was created as discoverable.

hints.description: Always empty — v1 gives the browser no authenticator hints.

PasskeyAuthenticationOptions.description: A bare `PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptionsJSON` — pass it straight to `navigator.credentials.get({ publicKey })`. Note `rpId` is flat here, unlike the nested `rp` object on registration options.

challenge.description: base64url challenge. Single-use, stored server-side for 5 minutes under `handle`.

allowCredentials.description: Always empty — sign-in is usernameless, so the browser offers whichever discoverable credential it holds for this `rpId`. Naming credentials here would leak which accounts exist.

PasskeyRegistrationResponse.description: The `PublicKeyCredential` returned by `navigator.credentials.create()`, JSON-serialized (base64url). Extra fields the browser adds (`clientExtensionResults`, `authenticatorAttachment`) are accepted and ignored.

id.description: base64url credential ID. Max 64 KB.

transports.description: Transport hints reported by the authenticator. Max 16 entries of 64 characters each.

PasskeyAuthenticationResponse.description: The `PublicKeyCredential` returned by `navigator.credentials.get()`, JSON-serialized (base64url). Extra fields the browser adds are accepted and ignored.

id.description: base64url credential ID. Max 64 KB.

userHandle.description: base64url. Max 64 KB. Ignored — the credential ID resolves the user.

id.description: The tenant identifier — caller-chosen and immutable once created. Composite primary key with `environment_id`, so the same value can exist independently in `development`, `staging`, and `production`. Free-form up to 255 characters: whatever you already use to identify a customer, including `/`, spaces and non-ASCII. The only values rejected are the ones no URL path segment can carry — control characters, leading or trailing whitespace, and the dot segments `.` and `..`.

environment_id.description: The environment this tenant belongs to.

name.description: Display name shown in the dashboard. Defaults to the tenant `id` on create if not supplied; can be edited later via `PATCH /tenant/{id}`.

metadata.description: Free-form JSON object stored verbatim. Truto does not interpret this field — use it for tier, region, billing plan, or any other customer attribute your app cares about.

created_at.description: The date and time when the tenant was created.

updated_at.description: The date and time when the tenant was last updated.

created.description: The tenants that were newly inserted.

updated.description: Tenants that already existed and were updated. Only populated when `mode` is `upsert`; always empty for `insert`.

skipped.description: Rows that were not inserted because a tenant with the same `(id, environment_id)` already existed. Only populated when `mode` is `insert` (the default), which uses `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`. Empty for `upsert`.

id.description: The tenant `id` that was skipped.

# Create link token
---
Link tokens allow your customers to connect their apps with Truto. Link tokens are used to initiate a connection flow handled by Truto and the end of this connection flow, an Integrated Account is created. This integrated account acts as a link between your Truto account and the app your customer has connected.
To create a link token, you need to specify a `tenant_id` in the request body. `tenant_id` references a [Tenant](/#tag/Tenants) — an environment-scoped external identity (your customer, workspace, or organisation) that owns one or more integrated accounts.
Truto auto-creates the tenant when an integrated account is first created with a given `tenant_id` (as long as the id can be carried in a URL path segment — see [Tenants](/#tag/Tenants)). Creating a link token alone does not materialize the tenant — the row appears after a successful connection (or a direct `POST /integrated-account`). If you'd rather attach `metadata` (tier, region, billing plan) before the customer connects, pre-create the tenant with `POST /tenant` first and use the same `id` here.
::: tip
One tenant can own multiple integrated accounts. For example, one of your customers could connect HubSpot, Salesforce, and Slack — all under the same `tenant_id` — and you can list every account for that customer with a single `GET /integrated-account?tenant_id=...` call.
:::
## Reauthorizing an integrated account
An integrated account can be reauthorized by creating a link token for it. Instead of `tenant_id`, you need to specify the `id` of the integrated account you need to reauthorize as the  `integrated_account_id` attribute in the request body. Do NOT specify `tenant_id`.
You can use it similar to other link tokens, with the only difference being that the customer will automatically land on the specific integration's page in Truto's connection UI and will be asked to proceed with connecting the application. After the connection flow completes, the new credentials will be updated in the integrated account.
## Custom OAuth Scopes
You can specify custom OAuth scopes using the `scopes` field for both new integrated accounts and when reauthorizing existing ones. These scopes will take precedence over any unified model scopes or integration default scopes during the OAuth flow. This is useful when you need to request additional permissions or restrict the scope of access for a specific integration.
## Environment Unified Models
You can specify one or more installed unified models using the `environment_unified_model_id` field. During the connection flow, Truto uses the OAuth scopes configured on those environment unified models for each integration. If you also specify `scopes`, those take precedence over the unified model scopes. This is useful when you want the connection to request permissions aligned with a specific unified API installation.
## Static Gate 
You can specify a static gate for an integrated account by providing the `truto_static_gate_id` field. When set, all outbound API requests made by this integrated account will be routed through the static gate's domain instead of directly to the Truto's API. This is useful for scenarios where you need to proxy requests through a specific domain or gateway. The static gate must be one you can see. For a link token that names an `environment_id`, it must also be in an environment of that environment's team, or it's a `404`. Whatever the token, a connection only ever uses a gate of its own team, and another team's gate is ignored when its requests are made.
This field is the only way to set the gate for a connection. Because it selects the host that every credentialed request for the account is sent to, `truto_static_gate_id` is ignored if it arrives in the connecting browser's own request — in the `context` it posts to complete the connection, or in the query string of the OAuth connect URL — on either a new connection or a reconnect. Set it here, where it is checked against your environment, and it is carried through the whole flow.

tenant_id.description: The ID of the tenant you want to create a link token for. Required if you are creating a link token for a new integrated account. Free-form up to 255 characters, excluding control characters, leading or trailing whitespace, and the dot segments `.` and `..`.

integrated_account_id.description: The ID of the integrated account you want to reauthorize. Do NOT specify `tenant_id` if you are reauthorizing an integrated account.

context.description: The context of the integrated account. You can find these in the `Variables` section of an integrated account in the Truto UI.

redirect_uri.description: The URI where the user should be redirected after the connection flow is complete. This is especially useful when you are authenticating via a Desktop app.

environment_unified_model_id.description: IDs of environment unified models (installed unified models) whose OAuth scopes should be used during the connection flow. When omitted, integration default scopes are used unless overridden by `scopes`.

scopes.description: OAuth scopes to request during authentication. These scopes will take precedence over unified model scopes and integration default scopes.

persist_previous_context.description: If set to true, the context of the integrated account will be persisted when reconnecting. Set to false by default.

truto_static_gate_id.description: The ID of the static gate to associate with this integrated account. The static gate must be one you can see. For a link token that names an `environment_id`, it must also be in an environment of that environment's team, or it's a `404`. Whatever the token, a connection only ever uses a gate of its own team, and another team's gate is ignored when its requests are made.

region.description: The region where the new integrated account will be placed. Only applies when creating a new integrated account via the link token (ignored for reauthorization).

400.description:
Malformed body — or, on reauthorization, an integration nothing can connect.

When `integrated_account_id` names an account whose integration has no usable authentication method left — every method it offers is a bring-your-own-app one (OAuth 2.0, AWS STS) with no app credentials configured in this environment — no link token is created, and the body carries `truto_error_code: app_credentials_not_configured` together with `integration`, `environment_integration_id` and `authentication_methods`. Add the credentials in the integration's settings, then retry. The account may reconnect with a different method, so an API key alongside an unconfigured OAuth app is not refused. A token minted with `tenant_id` alone is never refused for this reason; the connect flow leaves such integrations out of its catalogue instead.

403.description: The caller does not have access to the requested environment, or account creation is disabled.

404.description: The `integrated_account_id` is not one the caller can see.

# Create session token

---

A **session token** is a short-lived, tenant-scoped credential your backend mints for one of your customers and hands to their browser. It is what Truto's embedded connections widget runs on: the widget keeps the token in memory only and calls Truto directly with it, so your end users never hold an API key and your backend never has to proxy Truto traffic.

A session token is the lowest-trust credential this API issues. It is confined to a fixed allowlist of nine routes — `GET /environment-integration` (the catalog), `GET /integrated-account` (that tenant's connections), `GET /link-ui/{id}` (widget configuration and branding), `POST /link-token` (connect and reauth), `POST /integrated-account/refresh-credentials`, `POST /integrated-account/form-token` (reopen a post-connect form), `DELETE /integrated-account/{id}`, `POST /session-token/renew` and `GET /session-token/me` — and on every one of them the tenant and environment filters are forced from the token itself, never from anything the browser sends. Every other route answers `403`.

## Who may mint one

An API token or a signed-in dashboard user session. A session token cannot mint another one — that call is refused with `403`.

API-token callers may omit `environment_id`; it defaults to the single environment the API token is scoped to. User-session callers must send it, because a user can reach several environments and there is no safe default.

## Lifetime

`expires_in` is how long this token lives before it stops authenticating; `max_lifetime` is the wall no amount of renewing can move. The effective TTL is `min(expires_in, max_lifetime)`, so a `max_lifetime` smaller than `expires_in` shortens the first window rather than being ignored. Use `POST /session-token/renew` to slide the token forward, and `DELETE /session-token` as a kill switch.

## Narrowing the origins

`allowed_origins` may only ever *narrow* the list configured on the environment's Link UI — the result is the intersection of the two. Requested origins the environment does not already allow are dropped silently, so a typo (or an attempt to widen) fails closed instead of granting an origin nobody configured. An explicit `[]` is maximal narrowing and is honoured. Omit the field entirely to inherit the environment's list.

tenant_id.description: The tenant this session is scoped to. The tenant must already exist in the environment unless `create_tenant_if_missing` is true.

environment_id.description: The environment the tenant belongs to. Required for user-session auth. Defaults to the API token's own environment for API-token auth.

expires_in.description: Seconds until the token expires. Clamped to `max_lifetime` when that is smaller.

is_refreshable.description: Whether `POST /session-token/renew` may slide this token forward. A non-refreshable session must be re-minted instead.

max_lifetime.description: Seconds from issue until the absolute ceiling on this session. Renewal can never extend past it.

allowed_origins.description: Narrows the environment's allowed origins for this session only. Intersected with the environment's list — entries it does not already allow are dropped. Omit to inherit the environment's list.

create_tenant_if_missing.description: Create the tenant when it does not exist yet, instead of failing with `404`. Useful for first-run customers whose tenant row has not materialized.

201.description: The minted session token. This is the only time the secret is returned.

session_token.description: The session token. Send it in the `Authorization` header as a bearer token.

expires_at.description: When this token stops authenticating unless it is renewed.

max_lifetime_at.description: The absolute ceiling. No renewal can carry the session past this.

400.description: Missing or malformed body, a `tenant_id` outside the allowed pattern, an out-of-range `expires_in` / `max_lifetime`, or user-session auth without `environment_id`.

401.description: No credential, or an expired one.

403.description: The caller is not an API token or user session (a session token cannot mint another), or does not have access to the requested environment.

404.description: No such tenant in that environment, and `create_tenant_if_missing` was not set.

delete.description:
# Revoke session tokens

---

The kill switch. Revokes **every** live session token for one tenant in one environment, and only those — a tenant with the same id in another environment is untouched.

Revocation takes effect immediately: the next request made with a revoked token gets `401`, and renewal of it fails the same way.

Tenant *existence* is deliberately not required. Sessions outlive the row they were minted against, so revoking against a tenant that has since been deleted still works and simply reports how many live sessions it found. There is no `404` on this route — a tenant with no live sessions returns `200` with `"revoked_count": 0`.

tenant_id.description: The tenant whose sessions should be revoked.

environment_id.description: The environment to revoke in. Required for user-session auth. Defaults to the API token's own environment for API-token auth.

revoked_count.description: How many live sessions were revoked. Zero when the tenant had none.

400.description: Missing or malformed body, a `tenant_id` outside the allowed pattern, or user-session auth without `environment_id`.

401.description: No credential, or an expired one.

403.description: The caller is not an API token or user session (a session token cannot revoke its own family), or does not have access to the requested environment.

post.description:
# Renew session token

---

Slides a session token forward, performed by the session token itself — authenticate this call with the session token you want to renew. It takes no request body.

The secret is **not** rotated: the same `session_token` comes back with a later `expires_at`, so anything holding it keeps working and there is no grace window for in-flight requests to fall into. `max_lifetime_at` never moves — it is the ceiling renewal exists underneath.

Renewal is refused with `403` when the session was minted `is_refreshable: false`, and with a distinct `403` once the absolute lifetime is reached, so a client can tell "renew again later" from "start a new session". A token that has already expired or been revoked gets `401` — there is nothing left to renew.

session_token.description: The same secret that was sent in. Renewal does not rotate it.

max_lifetime_at.description: Unchanged from when the session was minted.

401.description: The session token is invalid, has expired, or has been revoked.

403.description: The caller is not a session token, the session was minted non-refreshable, or it has reached its maximum lifetime.

get.description:
# Introspect the current token

---

Describes the credential this request authenticated with. The envelope is deliberately token-kind-agnostic: `type` discriminates and `scope` is the per-type part, so an API token and a dashboard session get back the common fields only, while a session token also gets its scope, its clock, and its resolved `capabilities`.

Returning `capabilities` here is what keeps the embedded widget honest: the same resolved configuration backs every server-side gate, so a button the widget renders and the check that permits it cannot disagree.

It reports **counts, never values**, for anything sensitive. There is no `allowed_origins` array — echoing that list back into a browser would hand an attacker the exact string to spoof — only `allowed_origins_count`, which is the count of the list that actually governs this session (its own narrowing if it narrowed, otherwise the environment's). The token itself is never echoed either.

This is always a point read, so a revoked session reads as gone immediately rather than lingering in an index.

200.description: The current token. `type` and `id` are always present; everything else appears only for a session token.

type.description: Which kind of credential this is. `tenant` is a session token minted by `POST /session-token` — the credential this resource is named for. `api_token` is an admin API key, and `session` is a signed-in dashboard user, neither of which is a session token in the sense used here. An integrated-account token never appears: it cannot reach this route at all (see the `403` below).

id.description: The subject the credential resolves to — the tenant id when `type` is `tenant`, otherwise the API token id or the user id.

scope.description: Session tokens only. What this session is confined to.

issued_at.description: Session tokens only. When the session was minted.

expires_at.description: Session tokens only. Moves forward on every renewal.

max_lifetime_at.description: Session tokens only. Fixed at mint time.

is_refreshable.description: Session tokens only. Whether `POST /session-token/renew` will work.

issuer.description: Session tokens only. The credential that minted this session.

allowed_origins_count.description: Session tokens only. How many origins govern this session. The list itself is never returned. Zero means nothing may frame the widget.

team_name.description: Session tokens only. The name of the team that owns the environment — what the connect flow falls back to when the Link UI has no `brand_name`, so the widget can name the same party when it tells an end user who to contact.

capabilities.description: Session tokens only. The environment's resolved connections configuration — the same answer every server-side gate uses.

allow_connect.description: Whether the widget may start a new connection.

allow_reauth.description: Whether the widget may reconnect an existing account.

allow_refresh.description: Whether the widget may refresh an account's credentials.

allow_delete.description: Whether the widget may remove a connection.

allow_multiple_per_integration.description: Whether one tenant may hold more than one account per integration.

show_error_details.description: Whether raw upstream error details are included in the widget's connection reads.

allow_configure.description: Whether the widget may reopen an existing connection's post-connect form via `POST /integrated-account/form-token`.

layout.description: Session tokens only. The environment's presentation defaults for the catalog. Not a security boundary — the SDK may override them per embed and the end user may change them in the widget's own toolbar — but they belong to the environment, so they arrive with the session rather than being guessed client-side.

default_view.description: Which catalog layout the widget opens in.

default_group_by.description: How the catalog is grouped when it opens.

show_search.description: Whether the catalog's search box is shown. A catalog small enough not to need it hides the toolbar anyway.

401.description: No credential, or one that has expired or been revoked.

403.description: An integrated-account token was used — that credential is confined to its own routes.

get.description:
# Get widget frame ancestors

---

The list of origins allowed to embed an environment's connections widget, in the form the hosting edge turns into a `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors` header. Configure the list on the environment's Link UI; this endpoint is the read side of it.

**This endpoint is unauthenticated by design.** The edge that serves the widget document holds no credential — the whole point of the widget's handshake is that no token ever rides in the iframe URL — so this route has to answer without one. What it discloses is a list of public websites, strictly less than the `frame-ancestors` header it becomes, which any visitor to the widget can already read.

It **always** returns `200`. An unknown, unconfigured or malformed environment id returns an empty list rather than a `404`, so the route cannot be used to enumerate which environments exist. An empty list means the edge emits `frame-ancestors 'self'` — its fail-closed default, so an environment nobody has configured is framable only by the dashboard's own origin. `'self'` rather than `'none'` because the dashboard's settings page frames the widget document to preview it; doing so still needs a page on that exact origin *and* the ability to mint a tenant session, which already implies access to the same data.

Responses are cacheable for 60 seconds, which is short enough that an origin change propagates within a minute and long enough that the edge does not re-query on every iframe load.

`integration_override` is checked as on `PATCH`: while it keeps the environment's or integration's secret (it sends none of its own), it may move a host that secret is sent to only within its site or to a host one of the integration's select options gives, and may not change such a path (`auth.tokenPath`, `auth.refreshPath`, `auth.revokePath`, or the path of an OAuth 1.0a URL); any other move is a `400`.

Called with an API key, the `context` object comes back with every credential redacted.

Called with an integrated account token — as `GET /integrated-account/me`, the only id such a token may use — how much of `context` you get depends on how that token was minted:

- a token from `POST /integrated-account/token` receives the decrypted credentials in full;
- a token returned by a connection flow to the connecting browser receives none, except `context.oauth.token.access_token` for an integration whose browser file picker requires it (Google Drive, Box). A `refresh_token` is never returned to such a token;

patch.description:
# Update integrated account
---
You can use this endpoint to update an integrated account.

`integration_override` replaces the stored override, but the credential secrets under it that you leave out are kept. Send `null` to clear one, or `integration_override: {}` to clear them all. A credential you leave out of a `credentials` object you do send is removed, secrets included. An edit that drops the id stored beside a secret (`client.id`, an AWS `signing.access_key_id`, or a JWT `signing.id`), or changes or adds a `client.id` or `signing.access_key_id`, clears that secret too, so the account falls back to the environment's or integration's app as a whole. An edit that keeps that id but changes, adds or leaves out a URL a stored secret is sent to (`auth.tokenHost`, `auth.tokenPath`, `auth.refreshPath` or `auth.revokePath`, OAuth 1.0a's `auth.requestTokenUrl` / `auth.tokenUrl`, or the AWS STS `auth.tokenHost`), with the secret left out or sent as `********`, is refused with a `400`: send the secret with the new URL. A secret stored as one bare placeholder (`{{client_secret}}`, `{{environment_variables.x}}`), filled when the request is made, isn't held to its URLs; any other template (a default, a type, a fallback, spaces, or text beside it) is. An edit that also drops the id, or changes a `client.id` or `signing.access_key_id`, clears the secret instead; a JWT key beside a changed `signing.id` is refused like one beside the same id. To move an account to another app or host, send the secret with it. The environment's or integration's secret stays where it is sent: an override that sends none of its own (`********` is not its own) may move such a host only within the site it names (`test.salesforce.com` for `login.salesforce.com`) or to a host one of its select options gives, and may not change such a path (`auth.tokenPath`, `auth.refreshPath`, `auth.revokePath`, or the path of an OAuth 1.0a URL); any other edit to them is refused with a `400`.

The credentials stored in `context` are protected here: `context.oauth` is always kept as stored, and for a connect-flow integrated account token every other credential field is kept as stored too — so a browser that reads its account and writes the result back cannot blank a secret it was not shown. Use `PATCH /integrated-account/{id}/credentials` to change credentials.

A connect-flow integrated account token may send only `context`. Any other top-level field — `status`, `tenant_id`, `unified_model_override`, `integration_override` and the rest — is refused with `400`, naming the fields to remove, and nothing is written. `context.truto_static_gate_id` is kept as stored for such a token as well: it selects the host every request for the account is sent to, so it is not a browser's to change. `context` must itself be a JSON object for such a token — an array or a scalar is refused with `400` rather than merged, because a non-object cannot carry the stored credential fields forward. A token from `POST /integrated-account/token`, an API key and a dashboard session are all unaffected.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the integrated account you want to update.

400.description: A missing or malformed body, an attempt to change `region`, or — for a connect-flow integrated account token — any top-level field other than `context`. Nothing is written in any of these cases.

post.description:
# Bulk delete integrated accounts

---

This endpoint is polymorphic and supports two mutually exclusive modes:

**1. Synchronous mode** — `{ ids | tenant_id }`
Delete up to 1000 integrated accounts immediately and return the result.
Provide exactly one of:
- `tenant_id` — deletes accounts owned by that [tenant](/#tag/Tenants) in the environment. Capped at 1000 per request; if the tenant has more, repeat the call until `matched_count < 1000`.
- `ids` — deletes a specific list of integrated account UUIDs (max 99). The query uses `WHERE environment_id = ? AND id IN (...)`, so the parameter count is 1 (environment) + ids.length. D1 allows at most 100 bound parameters per query.

Session-authenticated requests must also send `environment_id` (query or body) so Truto knows which environment to scope the delete to. API tokens are already scoped to one environment.

**2. Legacy async mode** — `{ query, dry_run? }`
Enqueue a batch job that deletes accounts matching an arbitrary list filter. Results arrive via `batch_job:*` webhook events. This mode is preserved for backward compatibility with existing callers.

The endpoint detects the mode from the request body: if `query` or `dry_run` is present, it uses the async path; otherwise it expects `ids` or `tenant_id` and uses the synchronous path. If neither mode is identifiable, the request returns 400.

## Examples

### Synchronous: delete every integrated account for a tenant

```json
{
  "tenant_id": "acme-1"
}
```

### Synchronous: delete a specific list of integrated accounts

```json
{
  "ids": [
    "79a39d69-e27e-49cb-b9a9-79f5eea7aa26",
    "0c74a4ad-7b8e-4f3a-9c1d-2e4f5a6b7c8d"
  ]
}
```

### Async: delete matching accounts via batch job

```json
{
  "query": { "tenant_id": "acme-1", "status": { "ne": "active" } },
  "dry_run": false
}
```

tenant_id.description: Delete integrated accounts owned by this tenant in the environment. Capped at 1000 accounts per request; repeat the call until `matched_count < 1000` if the tenant has more. Mutually exclusive with `ids`.

ids.description: Specific integrated account ids to delete (max 99). The query uses `WHERE environment_id = ? AND id IN (...)`, so the parameter count is 1 (environment) + ids.length. D1 allows at most 100 bound parameters per query. Mutually exclusive with `tenant_id`.

environment_id.description: Required for session-auth requests (dashboard). API tokens are already environment-scoped and can omit this.

query.description: Arbitrary list filter for integrated accounts. Supports the same filters as the List endpoint. Must be non-empty.

dry_run.description: When true, the batch job reports what it would delete without actually deleting.

environment_id.description: Required for session-auth requests (dashboard). API tokens are already environment-scoped and can omit this.

matched_count.description: Number of integrated accounts that matched the filter.

deleted_count.description: Number of integrated accounts actually deleted. May be less than `matched_count` if accounts were deleted concurrently.

post.description:
# Create integrated account token
---
Integrated account tokens allow you to create an API Key of sorts which is scoped to a particular integrated account.

The most common use case for an integrated account token is to show the RapidForm UI to the user after they have already connected an account while back, to make some changes to their selections.

Integrated account tokens can be used similar to your Truto API Key by adding them to the Authorization header with Bearer token format.

Integrated account tokens support the following endpoints,
- `ALL /proxy` (Proxy API)
- `ALL /unified` (Unified API)
- `POST /link-token/post-connect-form`
- `GET /integrated-account/me`
- `PATCH /integrated-account/me`
Integrated account tokens are valid for 15 minutes.

## Reading the stored credentials

A token minted by **this** endpoint is a backend credential, and `GET /integrated-account/me` answers it with the account's decrypted upstream credentials in the `context` object — the OAuth `access_token` and `refresh_token`, API keys, and so on.

Truto mints the same token *type* at the end of a connection flow and returns it to the connecting browser (as `integrated_account_session_token`) so the Link SDK can finish setting the account up. **Those tokens do not read credentials.** They are answered with the same redacted `context` every other caller gets, except that an integration whose browser file picker cannot work without it — currently Google Drive and Box, whose picker SDKs take the token client-side — also receives `context.oauth.token.access_token`. A `refresh_token` is never returned to a connect-flow token, whatever the integration.

So: treat a token from this endpoint as equivalent to an API key for that one account, keep it server-side, and do not pass it to a browser. If a browser needs one, use the token the connect flow already gave it.

integrated_account_id.description: The ID of the integrated account you want to scope the token to.

integrated_account_token.description: The integrated account token that can be used to make API calls.

post.description:
# Refresh credentials for an integrated account
---
For integrated accounts that support it, you can use this endpoint to manually refresh the credentials for an integrated account.
Manually refreshing the credentials is NOT necessary in most cases. Truto automatically refreshes the credentials for an integrated account whenever a proxy or unified API request is made to the integrated account and the credential is about to expire within a minute or has already expired.

id.description: The ID of the integrated account you want to refresh the credentials for.

post.description:
# Refresh the mapping cache
---
Truto caches the resolved unified models, unified mappings and integration configurations that every unified and proxy API request reads, so those requests do not have to fetch them again on each call. That cache expires on a timer, so an edit becomes visible on its own within roughly 23 minutes without calling anything.
Call this endpoint right after editing a unified model, a unified mapping, or an integration's resources / API paths to cut that wait short.
**This is best-effort.** It clears Truto's shared cache and the per-connection caches in the environment. It cannot purge Cloudflare's per-region edge cache, so a region already holding a copy can keep serving the previous value for up to roughly 6 minutes. A request that was already reading the previous value when the refresh ran can also put it back into the shared cache as it finishes. That, and the per-connection clears continuing in the background, is why the response is `202 Accepted` rather than `200 OK`.
Pass `integration_id` when the edit was to that integration — its configuration, its API paths, or one of its mappings. Only that integration's connections can hold the affected entries, so naming it keeps the work proportional. Omit it after editing a unified model itself, which every connection in the environment caches.
`integration_id` is also **required** to clear that integration's cached configuration. That entry is not scoped to an environment, so a call without `integration_id` cannot identify it and leaves it cached until it expires on its own. Unified models and unified mappings are cleared either way.

environment_id.description: The environment whose cache to refresh. Optional when authenticating with an API token, which is already scoped to one environment — required otherwise.

integration_id.description: Restrict the per-connection clears to this integration's connections, and also drop its cached integration configuration. Must be an integration installed in this environment.

202.description: Accepted. The shared cache has been cleared; the per-connection clears are in progress.

environment_id.description: The environment the refresh was applied to.

integration_id.description: The integration the refresh was narrowed to, if any.

deleted_cache_key_count.description: How many shared cache entries were deleted.

cache_keys_truncated.description: True when the sweep did not finish — some shared entries are still cached and will expire on their own. Call again to continue.

integrated_account_count.description: How many of the environment's connections are having their per-connection cache cleared.

integrated_accounts_truncated.description: True when the environment has more connections than one refresh covers, so some keep their cached copy until it expires.

message.description: The same caveat in prose, safe to surface to a user.

400.description: environment_id is required and could not be inferred from the credential.

403.description: Forbidden — you do not have access to this environment.

404.description: The integration named by integration_id is not installed in this environment.

post.description:
# Create a post-connect form token
---
**Session tokens only.** Every other credential is refused with `403` — an API token or dashboard session already has `POST /integrated-account/token`, and this route exists precisely because that one is too powerful to expose to a browser.

Mints a **purpose-limited** integrated account token so the embedded connections widget can reopen an existing connection's post-connect form. Unlike an ordinary integrated account token, the token this returns is narrowed at the auth layer to exactly what rendering and submitting one form takes — `GET` and `POST /link-token/post-connect-form`, plus `GET /integrated-account/me` for its own account — and nothing else. It cannot reach `/proxy`, `/unified`, `/custom`, and it cannot `PATCH /integrated-account/me`. It lives for **10 minutes** and cannot be refreshed.

`GET /integrated-account/me` answers it with the credentials redacted, except `context.oauth.token.access_token` for an integration whose browser file picker requires it (Google Drive, Box). A `refresh_token` is never returned to this token.

The connection must belong to the session's own tenant — any other account answers `404`, the same as one that does not exist — and the integration must still define a `post_connect_user_form` action. Requires `connections.allow_configure` on the environment's `link_ui` config, which is **off by default**.

Rate limited to 5 requests per minute per session.

integrated_account_id.description: The connection whose post-connect form should be reopened. Must belong to this session's tenant.

integrated_account_token.description: The purpose-limited token. Keep it in memory; never put it in a URL.

403.description: Not a session token, or `connections.allow_configure` is not enabled for this environment.

404.description: The connection does not belong to this tenant, or the integration has no post-connect form.

429.description: Too many requests for this session.

post.description:
# Run post install actions for an integrated account
---
Some integrations require more information from the API to work. Truto runs some steps after an integrated account is connected and runs them. These can include things like making a request to the API and store some part of the response in the context attribute of the integrated account (Variables section).
This happens automatically when the integrated account is connected. But if you ever want to run it manually, then use this API.
An integrated account created with `POST /integrated-account` whose authentication method declares an `rsa_key_pair` generated field is the exception: the provider cannot have the key Truto just made, so the post-install and validation actions wait. Install the public key from the create response (`context.<name>`) with the provider, then call this endpoint.

id.description: The ID of the integrated account you want to the post install actions for.

post.description:
# Re-run an integration's validation steps against a live connection
---
Runs the integration's `validation` action immediately and answers with what each step found.
Validation otherwise runs once, when the account is connected, which makes `status` and `last_error` a record of how the connection looked that day. A credential revoked afterwards leaves an account reading `active` until something happens to call the provider. This endpoint is what makes that pair worth polling.
It writes the same `status` and fires the same webhook as the connect-time run, so a reader cannot tell the two apart. A failing run sets `validation_error` and emits `integrated_account:validation_error`; a passing run clears `validation_error` back to `active` and emits `integrated_account:active`.
Only `validation_error` is cleared. `needs_reauth` belongs to the credential-refresh path and `post_install_error` to the connect run — clearing either here would report a connection healthy on the strength of checks that never looked at what broke it.
Returns `404` when the integration declares no `validation` action.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The integrated account to validate.

200.description: The validation run completed. Check `success` for the outcome — a failing run is still a 200, because the request succeeded and the answer is that the connection is unhealthy.

steps.description: One entry per step, in the order they ran.

error.description: Present only when `success` is false. The failure that stopped the run, and the same value written to the account's `last_error`.

404.description: No such integrated account, or the integration declares no validation action.

# Send test event

Delivers a single event to one webhook so you can verify your endpoint receives, verifies and parses Truto events before wiring up the real thing.

The event is delivered **synchronously and directly** to the webhook — it reaches the endpoint whether or not the webhook subscribes to that event type, and the response tells you exactly how your endpoint answered. It is signed with the same `X-Truto-Signature` header as a production event and carries the webhook's real `environment_id`.

Pick an `event_type` and Truto generates a payload shaped like the one the platform really emits for it. Pass `integrated_account_id` to build that payload from one of your connected accounts (credentials are stripped, exactly as in production); leave it out and placeholder account data is used. `payload` is deep-merged over the generated payload if you need to pin specific values.

Calling with only `id` still works and sends `integrated_account:created`.

id.description: ID of the webhook you want to send the test event to.

event_type.description: The event type to simulate. Defaults to `integrated_account:created`.

integrated_account_id.description: Build the payload from this connected account instead of placeholder data. Must belong to the same environment as the webhook. Credentials are stripped before delivery.

payload.description: Values deep-merged over the generated payload, for pinning fields your handler branches on.

200.description: The event was delivered and your endpoint returned a success status.

event_type.description: The event type that was delivered.

payload.description: The payload that was delivered, after any overrides.

# List Logs
---
You can use this endpoint to list all the Unified, Proxy, Webhook and RapidBridge logs for your Truto account.
## Time Range Filtering
You can filter logs by time range using the `created_at` query parameter. This parameter accepts an object with `gt` (greater than) and `lt` (less than) properties, both in ISO format.
- If `created_at[gt]` is provided, `created_at[lt]` must also be provided
- The time range between `created_at[gt]` and `created_at[lt]` cannot exceed 1 month
- If `created_at[lt]` is not provided, it defaults to the current time
- If `created_at[gt]` is not provided, no time range filtering is applied

Example:
```json {
  "created_at": {
    "gt": "2024-03-01T00:00:00.000Z",
    "lt": "2024-03-15T00:00:00.000Z"
  }
} ```

The type of logs you want to filter by. The same value is echoed

# Create tenant

---

**Explicitly create a tenant** in the environment. Use this when you want to attach `metadata` (tier, region, billing plan) to a customer before they connect their first account.

If you skip this step and just connect an account (via `POST /link-token` then a successful connection, or a direct `POST /integrated-account`) with a new `tenant_id`, Truto auto-creates the tenant row when the integrated account is created (as long as the id can be carried in a URL path segment). Creating the link token alone does not materialize the tenant. The auto-created tenant has `name = id` and `metadata = {}`.

`id` must be unique within the environment — creating the same id twice returns `409 Conflict`. Use `POST /tenant/bulk` for idempotent batch inserts.

id.description: Your identifier for the tenant. Free-form up to 255 characters — `/`, spaces and non-ASCII are all fine. Control characters, leading or trailing whitespace, and the dot segments `.` and `..` are rejected. Immutable — cannot be changed later.

name.description: Display name. Defaults to `id` when omitted.

metadata.description: Free-form JSON object. Stored and returned verbatim.

environment_id.description: Which environment to create the tenant in. Required for session auth; ignored for API tokens (inferred from the token).

400.description: Invalid tenant id, missing `environment_id` on session auth, or invalid body.

409.description: A tenant with this `id` already exists in the environment.

post.description:
# Bulk create or upsert tenants

---

**Create or upsert up to 1000 tenants in a single request.** Use this for migrations from another platform, seeding staging with a known list of customers, or onboarding a batch of new tenants at once.

Each item may only include `id` (required), `name`, and `metadata`. Extra fields are rejected.

Set `mode` to control collisions on the composite `(id, environment_id)` primary key:

- `insert` (default) — `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`.
  Existing ids are reported in `skipped` with reason
  `already_exists`. Re-running the same request is idempotent.

- `upsert` — `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` for `name` and
  `metadata`. Existing rows are updated; omitted fields keep
  their current values. The response splits rows into `created`
  and `updated` (`skipped` is empty).


Internally the SQL is chunked into 25-row batches to stay within D1's 100-bound-parameter-per-query limit. Callers do not need to split the input; the 1000-item cap is still per request.

mode.description: Collision behaviour. `insert` skips existing ids; `upsert` updates `name`/`metadata` on existing ids.

tenants.description: The list of tenants to create or upsert. Max 1000 per request — split larger inputs client-side. Only `id`, `name`, and `metadata` are allowed per item.

id.description: Tenant id. Free-form up to 255 characters, excluding control characters, leading or trailing whitespace, and the dot segments `.` and `..`.

name.description: Display name. Defaults to `id` when omitted on insert; kept unchanged when omitted on upsert of an existing row.

metadata.description: Free-form JSON object. Defaults to `{}` when omitted on insert; kept unchanged when omitted on upsert of an existing row.

environment_id.description: Environment to create the tenants in. Required for session auth; ignored for API tokens. Applied to every row in the batch — the endpoint does not let you mix environments in one request.

400.description: Request body violates the schema (missing `tenants`, more than 1000 items, invalid tenant id, unknown fields, invalid `mode`, missing `environment_id` on session auth).

---

**Delete a tenant** by id. This is permanent — the row is gone and cannot be restored (re-creating the same id yields a fresh row with no metadata).

The API refuses to delete a tenant that still owns any integrated accounts, returning `409 Conflict` with the message _"Can't delete tenant with connected accounts."_. Delete the accounts first (individually via `DELETE /integrated-account/{id}`, or in one call via `POST /integrated-account/bulk-delete` with `{"tenant_id":"..."}`), then retry.

Session callers must pass `?environment_id=<uuid>` — the API will not guess which environment's row to delete.

Tenant ids are free-form and may contain `/`, spaces or non-ASCII, so reserved characters have to be escaped: `acme/prod` is requested as `/tenant/acme%2Fprod`. Sent raw, it is two path segments, matches no route, and comes back 404. Only *unreserved* escapes are normalised before the request reaches the API, so `%2F` arrives intact and is decoded back to the original id.

parameters.description: Required for session auth. Ignored for API tokens.

400.description: Session auth without `environment_id`.

409.description: Tenant still has connected integrated accounts.

# Update Environment Integration
---
**Update an existing environment integration**.   This can update fields like `show_in_catalog`, `is_enabled`, or `override`. You have the flexibility to customize an Integration and its configuration to better suit your specific needs. Customizing integrations allows you to override default settings, add new functionalities, and tailor the integration to fit seamlessly within your environment.  Read more about [Installing Integrations](https://truto.one/docs/guides/integrations/overview#installing-an-integration)

`override` replaces the stored override, so send the complete object. Secrets under it that you leave out are kept: credential secrets such as `client.secret`, and environment variables whose name ends in `_secret` when you don't send `environment_variables`. A secret sent back as `********` is kept too. Send `null` to clear one secret, or `override: {}` to clear everything. A credential you leave out of a `credentials` object you do send is removed, secrets included. An edit that drops the id stored beside a secret (`client.id`, an AWS `signing.access_key_id`, or a JWT `signing.id`), or changes or adds a `client.id` or `signing.access_key_id`, clears that secret too, so the environment falls back to the integration's app as a whole. An edit that keeps that id but changes, adds or leaves out a URL a stored secret is sent to (`auth.tokenHost`, `auth.tokenPath`, `auth.refreshPath` or `auth.revokePath`, OAuth 1.0a's `auth.requestTokenUrl` / `auth.tokenUrl`, or the AWS STS `auth.tokenHost`), with the secret left out or sent as `********`, is refused with a `400`: send the secret with the new URL. A secret stored as one bare placeholder (`{{client_secret}}`, `{{environment_variables.x}}`), filled when the request is made, isn't held to its URLs; any other template (a default, a type, a fallback, spaces, or text beside it) is. An edit that also drops the id, or changes a `client.id` or `signing.access_key_id`, clears the secret instead; a JWT key beside a changed `signing.id` is refused like one beside the same id. To switch to another app or host, send the secret with it. The integration's secret stays where it is sent: an override that sends none of its own (`********` is not its own) may move such a host only within the site it names (`test.salesforce.com` for `login.salesforce.com`) or to a host one of its select options gives, and may not change such a path (`auth.tokenPath`, `auth.refreshPath`, `auth.revokePath`, or the path of an OAuth 1.0a URL); any other edit to them is refused with a `400`. Where an override keeps the integration's secret, each connect-form select the integration offers keeps to the integration's options: the override may offer fewer, options of its own are dropped, and a select it leaves out comes back.

parameters.description: The ID of the environment integration to update.

show_in_catalog.description: Whether to show this integration in the environment's catalog.

override.description:
An optional config override for the integration at environment level. Deep-merged on top of the base `integration.config`.

Credential secrets (an OAuth app's `client.secret`, a `jwt_bearer` or `aws_sts` signing key) are never returned, so a body that leaves one out, or sends it masked as `********`, keeps the stored value, unless it changes the id or a URL that secret belongs to (see the description above). Send `null` to remove a stored secret while keeping the rest of that credential's `config`, for example when reverting `client.id` to the base integration's value.

---
**Update an existing integration**.   This call supports updating config, category, beta status, and sharing policy.   A version mismatch (optimistic concurrency) will cause a `400 Bad Request` error.

`config` replaces the stored config, but credential secrets you leave out (`client.secret`, `signing.key`, `signing.secret_access_key`, `signing.session_token`) are kept, as is a secret sent back as `********`. A secret stored as one bare placeholder (`{{client_secret}}`, `{{environment_variables.x}}`), filled when the request is made, isn't held to its URLs; any other template (a default, a type, a fallback, spaces, or text beside it) is.

# Create SSO Connection
---
**Create a new SSO connection** for a team. The `client_secret` (OIDC relying-party secret) is write-only — it is encrypted at rest and never returned.

You can create a connection as an **inactive draft** (`is_active: false`) with an incomplete `config`. This is the recommended first step: create the connection, read back the generated SP values (SAML ACS URL / SP Entity ID at `/auth/saml/{id}/acs` and `/auth/saml/{id}/metadata`, or the OIDC callback at `/auth/oidc/{id}/callback`), configure those in your identity provider, then update the connection with the IdP details and activate it.

Activation is guarded: setting `is_active: true` requires a complete config — SAML needs `idp_sso_url`, `idp_entity_id`, and `idp_x509_cert` (or `idp_metadata_xml`); OIDC needs `issuer`, `client_id`, and a `client_secret`. Activating without them returns `400`.

`is_active`, `enforced` and `is_default` each accept `true`/`false` or `1`/`0`, as JSON or as the strings `"true"`, `"false"`, `"1"` and `"0"`; any other value returns `400`.

team_id.description: The ID of the team this connection belongs to.

protocol.description: The SSO protocol for this connection.

enforced.description: Whether SSO login is enforced for the connection's verified domains.

is_default.description: Whether this is the team's default SSO connection.

config.description: Non-secret protocol settings.

sign_authn_requests.description: SAML only — sign SP-initiated AuthnRequests with the SP key (HTTP-Redirect binding).

allow_idp_initiated.description: SAML only — accept unsolicited (IdP-initiated) responses at the ACS. Defaults to false (unsolicited responses rejected) when omitted.

idp_metadata_xml.description: SAML only — IdP metadata XML. When provided, the server parses it to populate idp_entity_id, idp_sso_url, and idp_x509_cert, then discards the raw XML (never stored or returned).

client_secret.description: The OIDC relying-party client secret. Write-only — encrypted at rest and never returned.

default_role.description: The role assigned to users provisioned through this connection.

default_environment_ids.description: Environment IDs that provisioned users are granted access to by default. Each item must be the ID of one of the connection's team's environments; another team's environment, one that doesn't exist, a nested array or any other value is a `400`.

400.description: Bad request if required fields are missing

403.description: Forbidden if the user is not an admin of the specified team

post.description:
# Start passkey registration

---

Issues the `PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptionsJSON` for `navigator.credentials.create()` and parks the challenge server-side for 5 minutes, keyed to the signed-in user. Starting a second registration invalidates the first.

**Session only.** An API token is rejected with 403, and so is a session that is impersonating another user — a credential enrolled under impersonation would outlive the support session and sign in as the user forever.

**Step-up required.** A passkey outlives logout, session revocation and a password reset, so a session cookie alone is not enough to add one: the caller must re-prove a factor the cookie does not carry. Send `{}` first — if the account holds a factor the call answers 400 with `step_up` naming which one (`totp` when the account has an authenticator app, `password` otherwise), and the ceremony is retried with that field filled in. Accounts with neither (magic-link and social-login users) succeed on the first call. Five failed attempts per user in 15 minutes answer 429.

totp_code.description: Current code from the authenticator app. Required when the account has TOTP enabled; the password is not accepted in its place.

password.description: Account password. Required when the account has one and no TOTP.

400.description: Step-up proof missing or wrong (body carries `step_up`), the per-user cap of 20 passkeys is already reached, unknown body keys, or a body that is not JSON.

403.description: Not a browser session, the session is impersonating, or the organization enforces SSO (non-staff).

404.description: Passkeys are not enabled for this environment.

429.description: More than 5 failed step-up attempts for this user in 15 minutes.

post.description:
# Finish passkey registration

---

Verifies the attestation from `navigator.credentials.create()` against the challenge issued by `registration/options`, then stores the credential. The challenge is **single-use**: a failed verification cannot be retried against it, and the ceremony has to be restarted.

`name` is trimmed; a blank string is stored as `null`. Credential material is never echoed back — the response carries the sanitized passkey only.

name.description: Optional label for the credential. Trimmed; blank becomes `null`.

400.description: Challenge expired or already used, wrong origin or rpId, user verification absent, malformed attestation, unknown body keys, or a base64url field over 64 KB.

403.description: Not a browser session, or the session is impersonating.

404.description: Passkeys are not enabled for this environment.

post.description:
# Start passwordless sign-in

---

Unauthenticated. Issues the `PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptionsJSON` for `navigator.credentials.get()` — usernameless, so `allowCredentials` is always empty and the endpoint reveals nothing about which accounts exist.

The challenge is parked under the returned `handle` for 5 minutes and the browser is pinned with an httpOnly `__Host-truto_sso_session_state` cookie; both are required by `authentication/verify`, so the client **must** send the request with `credentials: 'include'`. The browser-side ceremony timeout is 60 s, well inside the 5-minute server window; a failed verify needs a fresh call here.

Guarded by Turnstile and a per-IP budget of 30 calls per 60 seconds.

cf_token.description: Cloudflare Turnstile token from the sign-in page.

200.description: Sign-in options, plus the handle to echo back on verify. Also sets the `__Host-truto_sso_session_state` binding cookie (HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=None).

Set-Cookie.description: `__Host-truto_sso_session_state=<random>; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=None` — binds the ceremony to this browser. The `__Host-` prefix pins the cookie to the API host, so no other `*.truto.one` origin can plant one.

handle.description: Opaque key the challenge is stored under. Echo it on `authentication/verify`.

400.description: Missing or invalid `cf_token`, unknown body keys, or a body that is not JSON.

404.description: Passkeys are not enabled for this environment.

429.description: More than 30 calls from this IP in 60 seconds.

post.description:
# Finish passwordless sign-in

---

Unauthenticated. Consumes the challenge stored under `handle`, checks the binding cookie, resolves the credential to its owner, verifies the assertion with `requireUserVerification: true`, and mints a **full session** — no TOTP step, because a user-verified assertion is already two factors, the same reasoning that lets a SAML/OIDC login skip MFA.

Send with `credentials: 'include'` so the binding cookie set by `authentication/options` travels with the request, and so the `session` cookie in the response is stored.

The response carries no user — read `/user/me` afterwards.

Sign-count policy: a device-bound credential whose counter fails to advance is rejected and audited as a suspected clone. Synced (`multiDevice`) credentials are exempt, because their devices legitimately disagree about the counter.

Set-Cookie.description: `session=<token>; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax` — the full session, no MFA step. No `Domain`, so the cookie is pinned to this host.

400.description: Unknown body keys, a body that is not JSON, or a base64url field over 64 KB.

401.description: One generic failure for every cause — unknown or revoked credential, deactivated user, expired or already-used challenge, missing or mismatched binding cookie, wrong origin or rpId, user verification absent, bad signature, counter regression. Deliberately indistinguishable so the endpoint stays enumeration-safe.

403.description: The organization enforces SSO (non-staff). Returned only after the signature has verified, so only someone who genuinely holds the passkey learns this.

404.description: Passkeys are not enabled for this environment.

429.description: More than 20 failed attempts from this IP in 15 minutes. A successful sign-in clears the budget.
